angolan.name: Angolan cuisine
angolan.line: Angolan cuisine consists of several dishes popular among nationals and foreigners, a fusion of indigenous African and Portuguese influences.

chadian.name: Chadian cuisine
chadian.line: Chadian cuisine is the cooking traditions, practices, foods and dishes associated with the Republic of Chad.

congolese.name: Congolese cuisine
congolese.line: The cuisine of the Democratic Republic of the Congo varies widely, representing the food of indigenous people.

centrafrican.name: Centrafrican cuisine
centrafrican.line: Central African cuisine includes the cuisines, cooking traditions, practices, ingredients and foods of the Central African Republic.

equatorial guinea.name: Equatorial Guinea cuisine
equatorial guinea.line: The cuisine of Equatorial Guinea is a blend of the cuisines of the native peoples of this African country, including the Annobonese, the Bubi, the Fang, and the Kombe.

gabonese.name: Gabonese cuisine
gabonese.line: Gabonese cuisine comprises the cooking traditions, practices, foods and dishes associated with Gabon, a sovereign state on the west coast of Central Africa.

santomean.name: Santomean cuisine
santomean.line: Santomean cuisine comprises the cuisine, dishes and foods of São Tomé and Príncipe, a Portuguese-speaking island nation in the Gulf of Guinea, off the western equatorial coast of Central Africa.

burundian.name: Burundian cuisine
burundian.line: Burundi is situated in East Africa and has a territory full of mountains, savannas and agricultural fields, with forests in the surrounding rivers and waters.

comorian.name: Comorian cuisine
comorian.line: Comorian cuisine refers not only to dishes from the independent Indian Ocean nation of the Comoros but also those of the French overseas department of Mayotte in the same archipelago.

djiboutian.name: Djiboutian cuisine
djiboutian.line: Djiboutian cuisine is a mixture of Somali, Afar, Yemeni, and French cuisine, with some additional South Asian culinary influences.

eritrean.name: Eritrean cuisine
eritrean.line: Eritrean cuisine is based on Eritrea's native culinary traditions, but also arises from social interchanges with other regions.

ethiopian.name: Ethiopian cuisine
ethiopian.line: Ethiopian cuisine characteristically consists of vegetable and often very spicy meat dishes.

ethiopian jewish.name: Ethiopian Jewish cuisine
ethiopian jewish.line: Ethiopian Jewish cuisine is the cuisine of the Beta Israel.

kenyan.name: Kenyan cuisine
kenyan.line: The culture of Kenya consists of multiple traditions and trends without a single prominent culture identifying the country.

maasai.name: Maasai cuisine
maasai.line: The Maasai are an Eastern Nilotic ethnic group native to northern, central and southern regions of Kenya including northern Tanzania, near the African Great Lakes region.

malagasy.name: Malagasy cuisine
malagasy.line: Malagasy cuisine encompasses the diverse culinary traditions of the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar.

malawian.name: Malawian cuisine
malawian.line: Tea and fish are popular features of Malawian cuisine.

mauritian.name: Mauritian cuisine
mauritian.line: The cuisine of Mauritius reflects the island’s tropical environment and its long history of cultural diversity.

mozambican.name: Mozambican cuisine
mozambican.line: The cuisine of Mozambique represents a mixture of indigenous foods and cooking practices, coupled with outside influences from Indian Ocean trade and Portuguese colonization.

rwandan.name: Rwandan cuisine
rwandan.line: Rwandan cuisine differs from other East African cuisine by its greater plant-based ingredients and sauces, despite considerable overlap in ingredients.

seychellois.name: Seychellois cuisine
seychellois.line: Seychellois cuisine is the cuisine of the Republic of Seychelles, an archipelago country consisting of 115 islands off the Indian Ocean coast of Africa.

somali.name: Somali cuisine
somali.line: Somali cuisine is characterized by a history of maritime trade networks, nomadic culture, and a colonial influence.

sudanese.name: Sudanese cuisine
sudanese.line: Sudanese cuisine is greatly affected by the historical cross-cultural influences of Arab, Nubian, Egyptian, Turkish, Greek, and Levantine cuisine in Sudan.

south sudanese.name: South Sudanese cuisine
south sudanese.line: South Sudanese cuisine is based on grains.

tanzanian.name: Tanzanian cuisine
tanzanian.line: Following Tanganyika's independence and unification with Zanzibar, leading to the formation of the state of Tanzania, President Julius Nyerere emphasised a need to construct a national identity for the citizens of the new country.

zanzibari.name: Zanzibari cuisine
zanzibari.line: Zanzibari cuisine reflects several heterogeneous influences, as a consequence of the multi-cultural and multi-ethnic nature of Zanzibar's and Swahili heritage.

ugandan.name: Ugandan cuisine
ugandan.line: Ugandan cuisine consists of traditional and modern cooking styles, practices, foods and dishes in Uganda, with English, Arab, and Asian influences.

zambian.name: Zambian cuisine
zambian.line: Zambian cuisine offers a range of dishes, which primarily features nshima, a staple thick porridge crafted from maize flour, locally known as mealie meal.

zimbabwean.name: Zimbabwean cuisine
zimbabwean.line: Zimbabwe, officially the Republic of Zimbabwe, is a landlocked country in Southeast Africa, between the Zambezi and Limpopo River, bordered by South Africa to the south, Botswana to the southwest, Zambia to the north, and Mozambique to the east.

algerian.name: Algerian cuisine
algerian.line: Algerian cuisine is influenced by Algeria's interactions and exchanges with other cultures and nations over the centuries.

berber.name: Berber cuisine
berber.line: The Berber cuisine or Amazigh cuisine, though lacking a singular and standardized culinary framework, encompasses a diverse range of traditional dishes and influenced by the numerous flavours from distinct regions across North Africa.

egyptian.name: Egyptian cuisine
egyptian.line: Egyptian cuisine makes heavy use of poultry, legumes, vegetables and fruit from Egypt's rich Nile Valley and Delta.

libyan.name: Libyan cuisine
libyan.line: Libyan cuisine is a diverse culinary tradition shaped by Amazigh, Arab, Ottoman, and Mediterranean influences, reflecting both the country's geography and its historical interactions with neighboring cultures.

moroccan.name: Moroccan cuisine
moroccan.line: Moroccan cuisine is the cuisine of Morocco, fueled by interactions and exchanges with many cultures and nations over the centuries.

tunisian.name: Tunisian cuisine
tunisian.line: Tunisian cuisine, the cuisine of Tunisia, consists of the cooking traditions, ingredients, recipes and techniques developed in Tunisia since antiquity.

western saharan.name: Western Saharan cuisine
western saharan.line: Western Saharan cuisine comprises the cuisine of Western Sahara, a disputed territory in the Maghreb region of North Africa, bordered by Morocco to the north, Algeria to the extreme northeast, Mauritania to the east and south, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.

botswana.name: Botswana cuisine
botswana.line: The cuisine of Botswana is unique but shares some of its characteristics with other cuisines of Southern Africa.

eswatini.name: Eswatini cuisine
eswatini.line: The cuisine of Eswatini is largely determined by the seasons and the geographical region.

lesotho.name: Lesotho cuisine
lesotho.line: Basotho cuisine features African traditions and British influence.

namibian.name: Namibian cuisine
namibian.line: Namibian cuisine is the cuisine of Namibia.

south african.name: South African cuisine
south african.line: South African cuisine draws from the culinary traditions of the various communities that inhabit the country.

afrikaner.name: Afrikaner cuisine
afrikaner.line: South African cuisine draws from the culinary traditions of the various communities that inhabit the country.

benin.name: Benin cuisine
benin.line: Beninese cuisine involves many fresh meals served with a variety of sauces.

burkinabé.name: Burkinabé cuisine
burkinabé.line: Burkinabe cuisine, the cuisine of Burkina Faso, is similar to the cuisines in many parts of West Africa, and is based on staple foods of sorghum, millet, rice, fonio, maize, peanuts, potatoes, beans, yams and okra.

cape verdean.name: Cape Verdean cuisine
cape verdean.line: The cuisine of Cape Verde is a West African cuisine largely influenced by Portuguese, Southern and Western European and West African cuisine.

gambian.name: Gambian cuisine
gambian.line: Gambian cuisine mainly consists of Mandinka, Wolof, Serer, and Jola food, similar to neighbouring Senegal.

ghanaian.name: Ghanaian cuisine
ghanaian.line: Ghanaian cuisine is the cooking traditions of Ghana.

guinean.name: Guinean cuisine
guinean.line: Guinean cuisine, part of the larger West African cuisine, includes a variety of traditional dishes, sauces, and beverages.

guinea-bissauan.name: Guinea-Bissauan cuisine
guinea-bissauan.line: Bissau-Guinean cuisine is the traditional cuisine of Guinea-Bissau, a West African country located on the Atlantic Ocean.

ivorian.name: Ivorian cuisine
ivorian.line: Ivorian cuisine is the traditional cuisine of Côte d'Ivoire, and is based on tubers, grains, pig, chicken, seafood, fish, fresh fruits, vegetables and spices.

liberian.name: Liberian cuisine
liberian.line: Liberian cuisine refers to the cuisine of Liberia.

malian.name: Malian cuisine
malian.line: Cuisine in Mali includes rice and millet as staples of Mali, a food culture heavily based on cereal grains.

mauritanian.name: Mauritanian cuisine
mauritanian.line: The cuisine of Mauritania, including the culinary practices of Mauritania, has been influenced by Arab, Berbers and African peoples who have lived in and traversed the "stark" landscape marked with Sahara desert dunes in caravans.

niger.name: Niger cuisine
niger.line: The cuisine of Niger draws on traditional African cuisines.

nigerian.name: Nigerian cuisine
nigerian.line: Nigerian cuisine consists of dishes or food items from the hundreds of Native African ethnic groups that comprise Nigeria.

saint helenian.name: Saint Helenian cuisine
saint helenian.line: The island of Saint Helena has been influenced by several European powers, by the inhabitants, and the ships passing through, during its history.

senegalese.name: Senegalese cuisine
senegalese.line: The cuisine of Senegal is a West African cuisine that derives from the nation's many ethnic groups, the largest being the Wolof, Fula, and Serer.

sierra leone.name: Sierra Leone cuisine
sierra leone.line: Sierra Leonean cuisine consists of the cooking traditions and practices from Sierra Leone.

togolese.name: Togolese cuisine
togolese.line: Togolese cuisine is the cuisine of the Togolese Republic, a country in West Africa.

yoruba.name: Yoruba cuisine
yoruba.line: Yoruba cuisine refers to the numerous and diverse foods of the Yoruba people of Yorubaland.

latin american.name: Latin American cuisine
latin american.line: Latin American cuisine is the typical foods, beverages, and cooking styles common to many of the countries and cultures in Latin America.

native american.name: Native American cuisine
native american.line: Indigenous cuisine of the Americas includes all cuisines and food practices of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

inuit.name: Inuit cuisine
inuit.line: Historically, Inuit cuisine, which is taken here to include the Greenlandic, the Yupʼik and Aleut cuisines, consisted of a diet of animal source foods that were fished, hunted, and gathered locally.

tlingit.name: Tlingit cuisine
tlingit.line: Tlingit cuisine is the food and drink of the Tlingit people, an Indigenous group of people from Alaska, British Columbia, and the Yukon.

bermudian.name: Bermudian cuisine
bermudian.line: Bermudian cuisine blends British and Portuguese cuisine with preparations of local seafood species, particularly wahoo and rockfish.

canadian.name: Canadian cuisine
canadian.line: Canadian cuisine consists of the cooking traditions and practices of Canada, with regional variances around the country.

canadian chinese.name: Canadian Chinese cuisine
canadian chinese.line: Canadian Chinese cuisine is a cuisine derived from Chinese cuisine that was developed by Chinese Canadians.

greenlandic.name: Greenlandic cuisine
greenlandic.line: Greenlandic cuisine is traditionally based on meat from marine mammals, birds, and fish, and normally contains high levels of protein.

mexican.name: Mexican cuisine
mexican.line: Mexican cuisine consists of the food traditions of Mexico.

oaxacan.name: Oaxacan cuisine
oaxacan.line: Oaxacan cuisine is a regional cuisine of Mexico, centered on the city of Oaxaca, the capital of the eponymous state located in southern Mexico.

mesoamerican.name: Mesoamerican cuisine
mesoamerican.line: Mesoamerican cuisine has four main staples: maize, beans, squash and chili.

ancient maya.name: Ancient Maya cuisine
ancient maya.line: Ancient Maya cuisine was varied and extensive.

aztec.name: Aztec cuisine
aztec.line: Aztec cuisine is the cuisine of the former Aztec Empire and the Nahua peoples of the Valley of Mexico prior to European contact in 1519.

mexican-american.name: Mexican-American cuisine
mexican-american.line: Mexican-American cuisine is the cuisine of Mexican Americans and their descendants, who have modified Mexican cuisine under the influence of American culture and immigration patterns of Mexicans to the United States.

new mexican.name: New Mexican cuisine
new mexican.line: New Mexican cuisine is the regional cuisine of the Southwestern US state of New Mexico.

tex-mex.name: Tex-Mex cuisine
tex-mex.line: Tex-Mex cuisine, or New Tejano cuisine, or simply Tejano cuisine is a regional American cuisine that originates from the culinary creations of Tejano people inspired in Mexican culinary traditions.

midwestern american.name: Midwestern American cuisine
midwestern american.line: The cuisine of the American Midwest draws its culinary roots most significantly from the cuisines of Central, Northern and Eastern Europe, and Indigenous cuisine of the Americas, and is influenced by regionally and locally grown foodstuffs and cultural diversity.

minnesotan.name: Minnesotan cuisine
minnesotan.line: The cuisine of Minnesota refers to the food traditions, cooking techniques, dishes, and ingredients found throughout the state of Minnesota.

iron range.name: Iron Range cuisine
iron range.line: Iron Range cuisine refers to the cooking traditions and dishes of the Iron Range of Minnesota.

floribbean.name: Floribbean cuisine
floribbean.line: Floribbean cuisine refers to a fusion cuisine found in Florida with an emphasis on fresh regional ingredients and complex medleys of spices, especially strong flavors offset by milder ones.

louisiana creole.name: Louisiana Creole cuisine
louisiana creole.line: Louisiana Creole cuisine is a style of cooking originating in Louisiana, United States, which blends West African, French, Spanish, and Native American influences, as well as influences from the general cuisine of the Southern United States.

cajun.name: Cajun cuisine
cajun.line: Cajun cuisine is a subset of Louisiana cooking developed by the Cajuns, itself a Louisianan development incorporating elements of Native American, West African, French, and Spanish cuisine.

lowcountry.name: Lowcountry cuisine
lowcountry.line: Lowcountry cuisine is the cooking traditionally associated with the South Carolina Lowcountry and the Georgian coast.

southwestern american.name: Southwestern American cuisine
southwestern american.line: The cuisine of the Southwestern United States is food styled after the cooking of the Oasisamerican Native Americans, Hispanos of New Mexico, caballero, cowboys, hillbillies, and Mexican Americans.

texan.name: Texan cuisine
texan.line: Texan cuisine is the food associated with the Southern U.S. state of Texas, including its native Southwestern cuisine–influenced Tex-Mex foods.

western american.name: Western American cuisine
western american.line: The Western United States has its cuisine, distinct in various ways from that of the rest of the country.

california.name: California cuisine
california.line: California cuisine is a food movement that originated in Northern California, in the United States.

hawaiian.name: Hawaiian cuisine
hawaiian.line: The cuisine of Hawaii incorporates five distinct styles of food, reflecting the diverse food history of settlement and immigration in the Hawaiian Islands, primarily originating from Polynesian, North American and East Asian cuisines.

rocky mountain.name: Rocky Mountain cuisine
rocky mountain.line: Rocky Mountain cuisine is a cuisine of Alberta and British Columbia in Canada; Idaho, Colorado, Wyoming, Utah and Montana in the United States.

fusion.name: Fusion cuisine
fusion.line: Fusion cuisine is a cuisine that combines elements of different culinary traditions that originate from different countries, regions, or cultures.

american jewish.name: American Jewish cuisine
american jewish.line: American Jewish cuisine comprises the food, cooking, and dining customs associated with American Jews.

chinese american.name: Chinese American cuisine
chinese american.line: American Chinese cuisine, also known as Sino-American cuisine and often referred to in American English as simply Chinese food, is a derivative of Chinese cuisine developed by Chinese Americans.

filipino-american.name: Filipino-American cuisine
filipino-american.line: Filipino-American cuisine has been present in the United States since ever Filipinos first immigrated there, but only recently has Filipino food become more widely popular.

greek-american.name: Greek-American cuisine
greek-american.line: Greek-American cuisine is the cuisine of Greek Americans and their descendants, who have modified Greek cuisine under the influence of American culture and immigration patterns of Greeks to the United States.

italian-american.name: Italian-American cuisine
italian-american.line: Italian-American cuisine is a style of Italian cuisine adapted throughout the United States.

new american.name: New American cuisine
new american.line: New American cuisine, also known as Modern American cuisine or Contemporary American cuisine, is the wave of modernized cooking predominantly served at upscale fine dining restaurants in the United States, originating in the 1980s.

belizean.name: Belizean cuisine
belizean.line: Belizean cuisine is an amalgamation of all ethnicities in the nation of Belize and their respectively wide variety of foods.

costa rican.name: Costa Rican cuisine
costa rican.line: Costa Rican cuisine is known for being mostly mild, with high reliance on fruits and vegetables.

guatemalan.name: Guatemalan cuisine
guatemalan.line: Most traditional foods in Guatemalan cuisine are based on Maya cuisine, with Spanish influence, and prominently feature corn, chilies and beans as key ingredients.

honduran.name: Honduran cuisine
honduran.line: Honduran cuisine is a fusion of Mesoamerican, Spanish, Caribbean and African cuisines.

nicaraguan.name: Nicaraguan cuisine
nicaraguan.line: Nicaraguan cuisine includes a mixture of Mesoamerican, Chibcha, Spanish, Caribbean, and African cuisine.

panamanian.name: Panamanian cuisine
panamanian.line: Panamanian cuisine is a mix of Spanish, Indigenous, and African techniques, dishes, and ingredients, reflecting its diverse population.

salvadoran.name: Salvadoran cuisine
salvadoran.line: Salvadoran cuisine is a style of cooking derived from the nation of El Salvador.

argentine.name: Argentine cuisine
argentine.line: Argentine cuisine blends elements from the Indigenous peoples of Argentina who focused on ingredients such as humita, potatoes, cassava, peppers, tomatoes, beans, and yerba mate, and from Spanish cuisine brought during the colonial period.

bolivian.name: Bolivian cuisine
bolivian.line: Bolivian cuisine is the indigenous cuisine of Bolivia from the Aymara and Inca cuisine traditions, among other Andean and Amazonian groups.

brazilian.name: Brazilian cuisine
brazilian.line: Brazilian cuisine is the set of cooking practices and traditions of Brazil, and is characterized by African, European, Amerindian and Asian influences.

chilean.name: Chilean cuisine
chilean.line: Chilean cuisine stems mainly from the combination of traditional Spanish cuisine, Chilean Mapuche culture and local ingredients, with later important influences from other European cuisines, particularly from Germany, the United Kingdom and France.

colombian.name: Colombian cuisine
colombian.line: Colombian cuisine is a culinary tradition of six main regions within Colombia: Insular, Caribbean, Pacific, Andean, Orinoco, and Amazonian.

muisca.name: Muisca cuisine
muisca.line: Muisca cuisine describes the food and preparation the Muisca elaborated.

ecuadorian.name: Ecuadorian cuisine
ecuadorian.line: Ecuadorian cuisine is diverse, varying with altitude and associated agricultural conditions.

french guianan.name: French Guianan cuisine
french guianan.line: French Guianan cuisine or Guianan cuisine is a mixture of Creole, Bushinengue, and indigenous cuisines, supplemented by influences from the cuisines of more recent immigrant groups.

paraguayan.name: Paraguayan cuisine
paraguayan.line: Paraguayan cuisine is the set of dishes and culinary techniques of Paraguay.

peruvian.name: Peruvian cuisine
peruvian.line: Peruvian cuisine refers to the culinary and gastronomical traditions of Peru, which originated in the pre-Columbian indigenous populations in its three main geographical regions along the Pacific coast, the Andes and the Amazonian areas.

peruvian-chinese.name: Peruvian-Chinese cuisine
peruvian-chinese.line: Chifa is a Chinese Peruvian culinary tradition based on Cantonese elements fused with traditional Peruvian ingredients and traditions.

peruvian-japanese.name: Peruvian-Japanese cuisine
peruvian-japanese.line: Nikkei cuisine is a type of fusion cuisine that combines Japanese and Peruvian elements.

amazonian.name: Amazonian cuisine
amazonian.line: Amazonian cuisine includes the foods and preparation methods of various peoples in the Amazon jungle of South America, including the dishes they have popularized among neighbors.

arequipan.name: Arequipan cuisine
arequipan.line: Arequipan cuisine is the cuisine of Arequipa, a regional Peruvian cuisine.

inca.name: Inca cuisine
inca.line: Inca cuisine originated in pre-Columbian times within the Inca civilization from the 13th to the 16th century.

surinamese.name: Surinamese cuisine
surinamese.line: Surinamese culture has strong Asian, African and European influences.

uruguayan.name: Uruguayan cuisine
uruguayan.line: Uruguayan cuisine is a fusion of cuisines from several European countries, especially of Mediterranean foods from Spain, Italy, Portugal and France.

venezuelan.name: Venezuelan cuisine
venezuelan.line: Venezuelan cuisine is influenced by its European, West African, and indigenous traditions.

anguillan.name: Anguillan cuisine
anguillan.line: Anguillian cuisine is the cuisine of Anguilla, a British overseas territory in the Caribbean, one of the most northerly of the Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles.

antigua and barbuda.name: Antigua and Barbuda cuisine
antigua and barbuda.line: Antigua and Barbuda cuisine refers to the cuisines of the Caribbean islands Antigua and Barbuda.

bahamian.name: Bahamian cuisine
bahamian.line: Bahamian cuisine refers to the foods and beverages of the Bahamas.

barbadian.name: Barbadian cuisine
barbadian.line: Barbadian cuisine, also called Bajan cuisine, is a mixture of African, Portuguese, Indian, Irish, Creole, Indigenous and British background.

british virgin islands.name: British Virgin Islands cuisine
british virgin islands.line: Virgin Islander culture reflects the various peoples that have inhabited the present-day British Virgin Islands and U.S. Virgin Islands throughout history.

cayman islands.name: Cayman Islands cuisine
cayman islands.line: The Cayman Islands are a group of islands situated in the Caribbean Sea just between Cuba and Honduras.

caribbean chinese.name: Caribbean Chinese cuisine
caribbean chinese.line: Caribbean Chinese cuisine is a style of food resulting from a fusion of Chinese and West Indian cuisines.

cuban.name: Cuban cuisine
cuban.line: Cuban cuisine is largely based on Spanish cuisine with influence from Amerindian, African and other Caribbean cuisines.

dominica.name: Dominica cuisine
dominica.line: Dominica cuisine is the cuisine of the island nation of Dominica.

dominican republic.name: Dominican Republic cuisine
dominican republic.line: Dominican cuisine is made up of Spanish, Indigenous Taíno, Middle Eastern, and African influences.

haitian.name: Haitian cuisine
haitian.line: Haitian cuisine is a Creole cuisine that originates from a blend of several culinary styles that populated the western portion of the island of Hispaniola, namely African, French, Indigenous, Spanish, and Levantine influences.

jamaican.name: Jamaican cuisine
jamaican.line: Jamaican cuisine includes a mixture of cooking techniques, flavours and spices influenced by Amerindian, West African, Irish, English, French, Portuguese, Spanish, Indian, Chinese and Middle Eastern people who have inhabited the island.

montserrat.name: Montserrat cuisine
montserrat.line: Montserrat's national dish is goat water, a goat meat stew and served with crispy bread rolls.

puerto rican.name: Puerto Rican cuisine
puerto rican.line: Puerto Rican cuisine consists of the cooking style and traditional dishes original to Puerto Rico.

saint lucian.name: Saint Lucian cuisine
saint lucian.line: Saint Lucian cuisine is a combination of French, East Indian and British dishes.

trinidad and tobago.name: Trinidad and Tobago cuisine
trinidad and tobago.line: Trinidad and Tobago's cuisine is influenced by Indian-South Asian, West African, Creole, European, North American, Chinese, Amerindian, Latin American, and Levantine culinary styles.

turks and caicos.name: Turks and Caicos cuisine
turks and caicos.line: The Turks and Caicos Islands consist of 30 islands situated in the Atlantic Ocean, southeast of the Bahamas.

us virgin islands.name: US Virgin Islands cuisine
us virgin islands.line: Virgin Islander culture reflects the various peoples that have inhabited the present-day British Virgin Islands and U.S. Virgin Islands throughout history.

afghan.name: Afghan cuisine
afghan.line: Afghan cuisine is the set of foods and culinary styles which are associated with Afghan culture.

hazara.name: Hazara cuisine
hazara.line: Hazara cuisine or Hazaragi cuisine refers to the food and cuisine of the Hazara people in Afghanistan and western Pakistan.

pashtun.name: Pashtun cuisine
pashtun.line: Pashtun cuisine or Afghan cuisine refers to the cuisine of the Pashtun people and is covered under Afghan, Central Asian and South Asian cuisines.

balochi.name: Balochi cuisine
balochi.line: Balochi cuisine is the food and cuisine of the Baloch people native to the Balochistan region spanning Afghanistan, Iran, and Pakistan, as well as diaspora communities worldwide.

bashkir.name: Bashkir cuisine
bashkir.line: Bashkir cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Bashkirs.

bukharan jewish.name: Bukharan Jewish cuisine
bukharan jewish.line: Bukharan Jewish cuisine is the traditional cuisine originating from the Bukharian Jewish community of Central Asia, who now mostly reside in Israel and the United States.

dagestani.name: Dagestani cuisine
dagestani.line: Dagestan, officially the Republic of Dagestan, is a republic of Russia situated in the North Caucasus of Eastern Europe, along the Caspian Sea.

iranian.name: Iranian cuisine
iranian.line: Iranian cuisine comprises the culinary traditions of Iran.

caspian.name: Caspian cuisine
caspian.line: Caspian cuisine is a regional cuisine found in Northern Iran, primarily found in the Mazandaran, Gilan, Alborz, and Golestan provinces.

kurdish.name: Kurdish cuisine
kurdish.line: Kurdish cuisine consists of a wide variety of foods prepared by the Kurdish people.

kazakh.name: Kazakh cuisine
kazakh.line: The cuisine of Kazakhstan, also known as Kazakhstani cuisine, encompasses all traditional and modern cuisines of Kazakhstan.

koryo-saram.name: Koryo-saram cuisine
koryo-saram.line: Koryo-saram are ethnic Koreans of the former Soviet Union.

kyrgyz.name: Kyrgyz cuisine
kyrgyz.line: Kyrgyz cuisine is the cuisine of the Kyrgyz, who comprise a majority of the population of Kyrgyzstan.

tajik.name: Tajik cuisine
tajik.line: Tajik cuisine is a traditional cuisine of Tajikistan, and has much in common with Iranian, Afghan, Russian, Chinese, and Uzbek cuisines.

tatar.name: Tatar cuisine
tatar.line: Tatar cuisine is primarily the cuisine of the Volga Tatars, who live in Tatarstan, Russia, and surrounding areas.

turkmen.name: Turkmen cuisine
turkmen.line: Turkmen cuisine, the cuisine of Turkmenistan, is similar to that of the rest of Central Asia.

uyghur.name: Uyghur cuisine
uyghur.line: Uyghur cuisine is characterized by ingredients such as roasted mutton and beef, as well as kebab and rice dishes.

uzbek.name: Uzbek cuisine
uzbek.line: The cuisine of Uzbekistan, also known as Uzbek cuisine, encompasses all traditional and modern cuisines of Uzbekistan.

japanese.name: Japanese cuisine
japanese.line: Japanese cuisine encompasses the regional and traditional foods of Japan, which have developed through centuries of political, economic, and social changes.

ainu.name: Ainu cuisine
ainu.line: Ainu cuisine is the cuisine of the ethnic Ainu in Japan and Russia.

okinawan.name: Okinawan cuisine
okinawan.line: Okinawan cuisine is the food culture of Ryukyu Islands, Japan.

japanese regional.name: Japanese regional cuisine
japanese regional.line: Japanese cuisine has a vast array of regional specialities known as kyōdo ryōri in Japanese, many of them originating from dishes prepared using local ingredients and traditional recipes.

nagoya.name: Nagoya cuisine
nagoya.line: Nagoya cuisine is a Japanese regional cuisine of the city of Nagoya and surrounding region in Central Japan.

japanese chinese.name: Japanese Chinese cuisine
japanese chinese.line: Japanese Chinese cuisine, known as chūka ryōri or simply chūka, refers to Japanese-style Chinese dishes and the restaurants in Japan that serve them.

korean.name: Korean cuisine
korean.line: Korean cuisine is the set of foods and culinary styles which are associated with Korean culture.

korean chinese.name: Korean Chinese cuisine
korean chinese.line: Korean Chinese cuisine, also known as Sino–Korean cuisine, is a hybrid cuisine developed by the ethnic Chinese in Korea.

korean regional.name: Korean regional cuisine
korean regional.line: Korean regional cuisines are characterized by local specialties and distinctive styles within Korean cuisine.

korean royal court.name: Korean royal court cuisine
korean royal court.line: Korean royal court cuisine was the style of cookery within Korean cuisine traditionally consumed at the court of the Joseon Dynasty, which ruled Korea from 1392 to 1897.

korean temple.name: Korean temple cuisine
korean temple.line: Korean temple cuisine refers to a type of cuisine that originated in Buddhist temples of Korea.

north korean.name: North Korean cuisine
north korean.line: North Korean cuisine is the traditional culinary practices and dishes of North Korea.

sakhalin korean.name: Sakhalin Korean cuisine
sakhalin korean.line: Sakhalin Koreans are a group of ethnic Koreans on the island of Sakhalin, Russia.

south korean.name: South Korean cuisine
south korean.line: South Korea is a country in East Asia constituting the southern part of the Korean Peninsula.

vietnamese.name: Vietnamese cuisine
vietnamese.line: Vietnamese cuisine encompasses the foods and beverages originated from Vietnam.

beijing.name: Beijing cuisine
beijing.line: Beijing cuisine, also known as Jing cuisine, Mandarin cuisine and Peking cuisine and formerly as Beiping cuisine, is the local cuisine of Beijing, the national capital of China.

chinese imperial.name: Chinese imperial cuisine
chinese imperial.line: Chinese imperial cuisine is derived from a variety of cooking styles of the regions in China, mainly from the cuisines of Shandong and Jiangsu provinces.

henan.name: Henan cuisine
henan.line: Henan cuisine or Yu cuisine refers to the cooking styles of the Henan province in China.

northeastern chinese.name: Northeastern Chinese cuisine
northeastern chinese.line: Northeastern Chinese cuisine is a style of Chinese cuisine in Northeast China.

jilin.name: Jilin cuisine
jilin.line: Jilin cuisine is the regional cooking style of the Han Chinese with heavy influence from native Manchu, Korean, and Mongolian minorities in the Jilin Province of Northeastern China.

liaoning.name: Liaoning cuisine
liaoning.line: Liaoning cuisine is derived from the native cooking styles of the Liaoning Province in China.

manchu.name: Manchu cuisine
manchu.line: Manchu cuisine or Manchurian cuisine is the cuisine of Manchuria and Outer Manchuria.

shandong.name: Shandong cuisine
shandong.line: Shandong cuisine, more commonly known in Chinese as Lu cuisine, is one of the Eight Culinary Traditions of Chinese cuisine and one of the Four Great Traditions.

shanxi.name: Shanxi cuisine
shanxi.line: Shanxi cuisine, or Jin cuisine, is derived from the native cooking styles of Shanxi Province in China.

tianjin.name: Tianjin cuisine
tianjin.line: Tianjin cuisine, also known as Jin cuisine, refers to the native cooking styles of Tianjin, the largest port city in Northern China.

xuzhou.name: Xuzhou cuisine
xuzhou.line: The local cuisine in Xuzhou is a blend of many of the flavours of northern and southern China, as a result of the location of Xuzhou.

anhui.name: Anhui cuisine
anhui.line: Anhui cuisine, alternatively referred to as Hui cuisine, is one of the Eight Culinary Traditions of Chinese cuisine.

jiangsu.name: Jiangsu cuisine
jiangsu.line: Jiangsu cuisine, also known as Su cuisine, is one of the Eight Culinary Traditions of Chinese cuisine.

huaiyang.name: Huaiyang cuisine
huaiyang.line: Huaiyang or Jianghuai cuisine is one of the Four Great Traditions in Chinese cuisine.

shanghai.name: Shanghai cuisine
shanghai.line: Shanghai cuisine, also known as Hu cuisine, is a popular style of Chinese food.

haipai.name: Haipai cuisine
haipai.line: Haipai cuisine is a Western-style cooking that is unique to Shanghai, China.

zhejiang.name: Zhejiang cuisine
zhejiang.line: Zhejiang cuisine, alternatively known as Zhe cuisine, is one of the Eight Culinary Traditions of Chinese cuisine.

gansu.name: Gansu cuisine
gansu.line: Gansu cuisine, also known as Long cuisine, is the regional cooking style of the Han Chinese deeply influenced by the local Hui people in the Gansu province of Northwestern China.

qinghai.name: Qinghai cuisine
qinghai.line: Qinghai cuisine is the regional cooking style of the Han Chinese with distinct influence from the Hui, Monguor people, and Tibetans in the Qinghai province in Northwest China.

shaanxi.name: Shaanxi cuisine
shaanxi.line: Shaanxi cuisine, or Qin cuisine, is derived from the native cooking styles of Shaanxi Province and parts of northwestern China.

guilin.name: Guilin cuisine
guilin.line: Guilin, formerly romanized as Kweilin, is a prefecture-level city in the northeast of China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

guizhou.name: Guizhou cuisine
guizhou.line: Guizhou cuisine, or Qian cuisine, consists of cooking traditions and dishes from Guizhou Province in southwestern China.

hubei.name: Hubei cuisine
hubei.line: Hubei cuisine, also known as Chu cuisine or E cuisine, is derived from the native cooking styles of Hubei Province in China.

hunan.name: Hunan cuisine
hunan.line: Hunan cuisine, also known as Xiang cuisine, consists of the cuisines of the Xiang River region, Dongting Lake and western Hunan Province in China.

jiangxi.name: Jiangxi cuisine
jiangxi.line: Jiangxi cuisine, also known as Gan cuisine, is a style of Chinese cuisine derived from the native cooking styles of Jiangxi province in southern China.

sichuan.name: Sichuan cuisine
sichuan.line: Sichuan cuisine or Sichuanese cuisine, alternatively romanized as Szechwan cuisine or Szechuan cuisine is a style of Chinese cuisine originating from Sichuan province and the neighboring Chongqing municipality.

yunnan.name: Yunnan cuisine
yunnan.line: Yunnan cuisine, alternatively known as Dian cuisine, is an amalgam of the cuisines of Han Chinese and other ethnic minority groups in Yunnan province in southwestern China.

guangxi.name: Guangxi cuisine
guangxi.line: Guangxi cuisine is the cuisine of Guangxi, China.

hong kong.name: Hong Kong cuisine
hong kong.line: Hong Kong cuisine is mainly influenced by Cantonese cuisine, European cuisines and non-Cantonese Chinese cuisines, as well as Japanese, Korean and Southeast Asian cuisines, due to Hong Kong's past as a British colony and a long history of being an international port of commerce.

macanese.name: Macanese cuisine
macanese.line: Macanese cuisine is mainly influenced by Chinese cuisine, especially Cantonese cuisine, and European cuisine, predominantly Portuguese cuisine, and influences from Southeast Asia and the Lusophone world, due to Macau's past as a Portuguese colony and long history of being an international tourist gambling centre.

hakka.name: Hakka cuisine
hakka.line: Hakka cuisine is the cooking style of the Hakka people.

min.name: Min cuisine
min.line: Fujian cuisine or Fujianese cuisine, also known as Min cuisine, is one of the native Chinese cuisines derived from the cooking style of China's Fujian Province, most notably from the provincial capital, Fuzhou.

fuzhou.name: Fuzhou cuisine
fuzhou.line: Fuzhou cuisine is one of the four subsets of Fujian cuisine, which is one of the Eight Great Traditions of Chinese cuisine.

hainan.name: Hainan cuisine
hainan.line: Hainan cuisine, or Hainanese cuisine, is derived from the cooking styles of the peoples of Hainan Province in China.

putian (henghwa).name: Putian (Henghwa) cuisine
putian (henghwa).line: Putian cuisine, also known as Henghwa cuisine or Henghua cuisine, is a style of Chinese cuisine originating from the Putian people of Putian, Fujian Province.

chaoshan (teochew).name: Chaoshan (Teochew) cuisine
chaoshan (teochew).line: Teochew cuisine, also known as Chiuchow cuisine, Chaozhou cuisine or Teo-swa cuisine, originated from the Chaoshan region in the eastern part of China's Guangdong Province, which includes the cities of Chaozhou, Shantou and Jieyang.

ou.name: Ou cuisine
ou.line: Ou cuisine, alternatively known as Wenzhou cuisine, is one of the four schools of Zhejiang cuisine, whereas Zhejiang cuisine is one of the eight major cuisines in China.

taiwan.name: Taiwan cuisine
taiwan.line: Taiwanese cuisine is a popular style of food with several variations, including Chinese and that of Taiwanese indigenous peoples, with the earliest cuisines known of being the indigenous ones.

kachin.name: Kachin cuisine
kachin.line: Kachin cuisine is food indigenous to the Kachin peoples, who inhabit the northern areas of Myanmar, as well as parts of China and Arunachal Pradesh, associated with Kachin.

hmong.name: Hmong cuisine
hmong.line: Hmong cuisine comprises the culinary culture of Hmong people, an Asian diaspora originally from China who are present today in countries across the world.

mongolian.name: Mongolian cuisine
mongolian.line: Mongolian cuisine predominantly consists of dairy products, meat, and animal fats.

tibetan.name: Tibetan cuisine
tibetan.line: Tibetan cuisine includes the culinary traditions and practices of the Tibetan people in the Tibet region.

chinese buddhist.name: Chinese Buddhist cuisine
chinese buddhist.line: Buddhist cuisine is an Asian cuisine that is followed by monks and many believers from areas historically influenced by Mahayana Buddhism.

chinese islamic.name: Chinese Islamic cuisine
chinese islamic.line: Chinese Islamic cuisine consists of variations of regionally popular foods that are typical of Han Chinese cuisine, in particular to make them halal.

american chinese.name: American Chinese cuisine
american chinese.line: American Chinese cuisine, also known as Sino-American cuisine and often referred to in American English as simply Chinese food, is a derivative of Chinese cuisine developed by Chinese Americans.

australian chinese.name: Australian Chinese cuisine
australian chinese.line: Australian Chinese cuisine is a style of cooking developed by Australians of Chinese descent, who adapted dishes to satisfy local Anglo-Celtic tastes.

british chinese.name: British Chinese cuisine
british chinese.line: British Chinese cuisine is a style of Chinese cuisine developed by British Chinese people in the United Kingdom, typically adapted to British tastes but increasingly inspired by authentic Cantonese dishes.

burmese chinese.name: Burmese Chinese cuisine
burmese chinese.line: Burmese Chinese, also Sino-Burmese or Tayoke, are Burmese citizens of Han Chinese ethnicity.

cambodian chinese.name: Cambodian Chinese cuisine
cambodian chinese.line: Cambodian Chinese or Sino-Khmer cuisine is a food tradition developed by the Cambodian Chinese living in Cambodia that is distinct from both Khmer and Chinese cuisines.

filipino chinese.name: Filipino Chinese cuisine
filipino chinese.line: Filipino Chinese cuisine is a style of Filipino cuisine influenced by Chinese cuisine historically brought to the Philippines by Chinese Filipinos, starting with the Sangley Chinese and their Chinese mestizo descendants and modern descendants in the Chinese Filipino community of the Philippines.

indian chinese.name: Indian Chinese cuisine
indian chinese.line: Indian Chinese cuisine is a distinct style of Chinese cuisine adapted to Indian tastes and spices.

indonesian chinese.name: Indonesian Chinese cuisine
indonesian chinese.line: Chinese Indonesian cuisine (Indonesian: Masakan Tionghoa-Indonesia, simplified Chinese: 印尼中华料理; traditional Chinese: 印尼中華料理; pinyin: yìnní zhōnghuá liàolǐ or Tn̂g-lâng-chia̍k is characterized by the mixture of Chinese with local Indonesian style.

latin american chinese.name: Latin American Chinese cuisine
latin american chinese.line: Chinese Latin American or Chino-Latino cuisine, associated with Asian Latin Americans of Chinese origin, combines elements of Chinese cuisine with other Latin American influences.

puerto rican chinese.name: Puerto Rican Chinese cuisine
puerto rican chinese.line: Puerto Rican Chinese cuisine is a popular style of food exclusive to restaurants in Puerto Rico developed by its Chinese immigrants.

malaysian chinese.name: Malaysian Chinese cuisine
malaysian chinese.line: Malaysian Chinese cuisine is derived from the culinary traditions of Chinese Malaysian immigrants and their descendants, who have adapted or modified their culinary traditions under the influence of Malaysian culture as well as immigration patterns of Chinese to Malaysia.

new zealand chinese.name: New Zealand Chinese cuisine
new zealand chinese.line: New Zealand Chinese cuisine is a style of cooking developed by Chinese migrants who arrived to New Zealand.

pakistani chinese.name: Pakistani Chinese cuisine
pakistani chinese.line: Pakistani Chinese cuisine comprises the styles and variations of Chinese cuisine that are cooked and consumed in Pakistan.

peranakan.name: Peranakan cuisine
peranakan.line: Peranakan cuisine or Nyonya cuisine comes from the Peranakans, descendants of early Chinese migrants who settled in Penang, Malacca, Singapore and Indonesia, inter-marrying with local Malays.

bhutanese.name: Bhutanese cuisine
bhutanese.line: A staple of Bhutanese cuisine is Bhutanese red rice, which is like brown rice in texture, but has a nutty taste.

buryat.name: Buryat cuisine
buryat.line: Buryat cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Buryats, a Mongolic people who mostly live in the Buryat Republic and around Lake Baikal in Russia.

sikkimese.name: Sikkimese cuisine
sikkimese.line: Sikkimese cuisine is a collection of dishes representative of the Indigenous peoples of Sikkim.

russian.name: Russian cuisine
russian.line: Russian cuisine is a collection of the different dishes and cooking traditions of the Russian people as well as a list of culinary products popular in Russia, with most names being known since pre-Soviet times, coming from all kinds of social circles.

chukchi.name: Chukchi cuisine
chukchi.line: Chukchi cuisine refers to subsistence foods and their methods of preparation used by the Chukchi people, one of the indigenous peoples of Siberia.

sakha.name: Sakha cuisine
sakha.line: Sakha cuisine encompasses the customary and traditional cooking techniques and culinary arts of Sakha.

yamal.name: Yamal cuisine
yamal.line: Traditional Yamal cuisine is an important part of national culture of the Nenets, Khanty and Komi.

yup'ik.name: Yup'ik cuisine
yup'ik.line: Yup'ik cuisine refers to the Inuit and Yup'ik style traditional subsistence food and cuisine of the Yup'ik people from western and southwestern Alaska.

bangladeshi.name: Bangladeshi cuisine
bangladeshi.line: Bangladeshi cuisine has been shaped by the region's history and riverine geography.

bengali.name: Bengali cuisine
bengali.line: Bengali cuisine is the culinary style of Bengal, comprising now most of Bangladesh, Indian states of West Bengal, eastern part of Jharkhand known as Manbhum and a region of Assam known as Barak valley.

maldivian.name: Maldivian cuisine
maldivian.line: Maldivian cuisine, also called Dhivehi cuisine, is the cuisine of the Maldives and Minicoy, Lakshadweep, India.

nepalese.name: Nepalese cuisine
nepalese.line: Nepali cuisine comprises a variety of cuisines based upon ethnicity, alluvial soil and climate relating to cultural diversity and geography of Nepal and neighboring regions of Sikkim and Gorkhaland.

newari.name: Newari cuisine
newari.line: Newar cuisine, also referred to as Newari cuisine, is a subset of Nepalese cuisine that has developed over centuries among the Newars of the Nepal Mandala region in Nepal.

sri lankan.name: Sri Lankan cuisine
sri lankan.line: Sri Lankan cuisine is known for its particular combinations of herbs, spices, fish, vegetables, rices, and fruits.

goan.name: Goan cuisine
goan.line: Goan cuisine consists of regional foods popular in Goa, India.

goan catholic.name: Goan Catholic cuisine
goan catholic.line: Goan Catholic Cuisine is the cuisine of the Goan Catholic community and is largely influenced by Portuguese cuisine.

gujarati.name: Gujarati cuisine
gujarati.line: Gujarati cuisine is the cuisine of the Indian state of Gujarat.

maharashtrian.name: Maharashtrian cuisine
maharashtrian.line: Maharashtrian or Marathi cuisine is the cuisine of the Marathi people from the Indian state of Maharashtra.

malvani.name: Malvani cuisine
malvani.line: Malvani cuisine is the standard cuisine of the South Konkan region of the Indian states of Maharashtra and Goa.

parsi.name: Parsi cuisine
parsi.line: Parsi cuisine refers to the traditional cuisine of the Parsi people who had migrated into the Indian subcontinent from Persia, and currently spread across the modern-day South Asian republics of India and Pakistan.

rajasthani.name: Rajasthani cuisine
rajasthani.line: Rajasthani cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Rajasthan state in north-west India.

sindhi.name: Sindhi cuisine
sindhi.line: Sindhi cuisine refers to the traditional culinary practices of the Sindhi people, originating in the historical region of Sindh, along the lower Indus River in the northwestern Indian subcontinent, in present-day Pakistan.

north indian.name: North Indian cuisine
north indian.line: North Indian cuisine is collectively the cuisine of North India, which includes the cuisines of Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh.

bhojpuri.name: Bhojpuri cuisine
bhojpuri.line: Bhojpuri cuisine is a style of food preparation common among the Bhojpuri people of Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh in India, and also the Terai region of Nepal.

kashmiri.name: Kashmiri cuisine
kashmiri.line: Kashmiri cuisine is the traditional culinary practices of the Kashmiri people.

maithil.name: Maithil cuisine
maithil.line: Maithil cuisine, also known as Mithila cuisine, is the traditional cooking style of Maithils residing in the Mithila region of India and Nepal.

mughlai.name: Mughlai cuisine
mughlai.line: Mughlai cuisine consists of delicately-spiced dishes developed or popularised in the early-modern Indo-Persian cultural centres of the Mughal Empire.

punjabi.name: Punjabi cuisine
punjabi.line: Punjabi cuisine is a culinary style originating in the Punjab, a region in South Asia, which is now divided into an Indian part to the east and a Pakistani part to the west.

uttar pradesh.name: Uttar Pradesh cuisine
uttar pradesh.line: Cuisine of Uttar Pradesh is an umbrella term for various regional cuisines within the state of Uttar Pradesh located in Northern India.

awadhi.name: Awadhi cuisine
awadhi.line: Awadhi cuisine is a cuisine native to the Awadh region in northern India and southern Nepal.

south indian.name: South Indian cuisine
south indian.line: South Indian cuisine includes the cuisines of the five southern states of India— Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and the union territory of Lakshadweep.

karnataka.name: Karnataka cuisine
karnataka.line: Karnataka cuisine is the cuisine of the Indian state of Karnataka.

dakshina karnataka.name: Dakshina Karnataka cuisine
dakshina karnataka.line: South Karnataka generally refers to the southern part of Karnataka state, excluding the coastal areas.

kodava.name: Kodava cuisine
kodava.line: The Kodavas, also called Coorgs, are an endogamous Dravidian ethnolinguistic group from the region of Kodagu in the southern Indian state of Karnataka, who natively speak the Kodava language.

mangalurean catholic.name: Mangalurean Catholic cuisine
mangalurean catholic.line: Mangalorean Catholic cuisine is the cuisine of the Mangalorean Catholic community which is an important aspect of the culture of Mangalorean Catholics.

udupi.name: Udupi cuisine
udupi.line: Udupi cuisine is a cuisine of South India.

uttara karnataka.name: Uttara Karnataka cuisine
uttara karnataka.line: North Karnataka, is a geographical region in Deccan Plateau from 300 to 730 metres elevation that constitutes the north region of the Karnataka state in India and the region consists of 14 districts.

kerala.name: Kerala cuisine
kerala.line: Kerala cuisine is a culinary style that originated in Kerala, a state on the southwestern Malabar Coast of India.

tamil.name: Tamil cuisine
tamil.line: Tamil cuisine is a generic term used to describe culinary practices among Tamil-speaking populations, originating from Southern India and neighboring Sri Lanka.

chettinad.name: Chettinad cuisine
chettinad.line: Chettinadu cuisine is the cuisine of a community called the Nagarathars, from the Chettinad region in Sivaganga district of Tamil Nadu state in India.

telugu.name: Telugu cuisine
telugu.line: Andhra cuisine is the traditional culinary style of the Telugu people, who are native to the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

andhra.name: Andhra cuisine
andhra.line: Andhra cuisine is the traditional culinary style of the Telugu people, who are native to the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

hyderabadi.name: Hyderabadi cuisine
hyderabadi.line: Hyderabadi cuisine, also known as Deccani cuisine, is the cooking style characteristic of the city of Hyderabad and its surrounding area in Telangana, India.

north east indian.name: North East Indian cuisine
north east indian.line: Northeast India, officially the North Eastern Region, is the easternmost region of India representing both a geographic and political administrative division of the country.

assamese.name: Assamese cuisine
assamese.line: Assamese cuisine is the cuisine of the Indian state of Assam.

manipuri.name: Manipuri cuisine
manipuri.line: Manipuri cuisine refers to the cuisine of Manipur, a state of northeastern India.

meitei.name: Meitei cuisine
meitei.line: The Meitei people, also known as Meetei people, are a Tibeto-Burman ethnic group native to the Indian State of Manipur.

mizo.name: Mizo cuisine
mizo.line: Mizo cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Mizo people of Mizoram, India.

naga.name: Naga cuisine
naga.line: Naga cuisine consists of foods from or commonly eaten by the Naga people in Northeast India and Kachin, Sagaing Region of Myanmar, or by the Naga diaspora.

tripuri.name: Tripuri cuisine
tripuri.line: Tripuri cuisine is the type of traditional foods of the Tripuri/Tiprasa people served in the northeastern region of India and Bangladesh.

jharkhandi.name: Jharkhandi cuisine
jharkhandi.line: Jharkhandi cuisine is the cuisine of the Indian state of Jharkhand.

odia.name: Odia cuisine
odia.line: The cuisine of Odisha is the cuisine of the Indian state of Odisha.

oriya.name: Oriya cuisine
oriya.line: The cuisine of Odisha is the cuisine of the Indian state of Odisha.

anglo-indian.name: Anglo-Indian cuisine
anglo-indian.line: Anglo-Indian cuisine is the cuisine that developed during British rule in India, between 1612 and 1947, and has survived into the 21st century.

jain.name: Jain cuisine
jain.line: Jain vegetarianism is the mandatory, spiritually motivated diet practiced by the followers of Jainism.

malaysian indian.name: Malaysian Indian cuisine
malaysian indian.line: Malaysian Indian cuisine, or the cooking of the ethnic Indian communities in Malaysia, consists of adaptations of authentic dishes from India, as well as original creations inspired by the diverse food culture of Malaysia.

muhajir.name: Muhajir cuisine
muhajir.line: Karachi cuisine refers to the cuisine found mainly in the city of Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan.

lahori.name: Lahori cuisine
lahori.line: Lahori cuisine refers to the food and cuisine of the city of Lahore in Punjab, Pakistan.

saraiki.name: Saraiki cuisine
saraiki.line: Saraiki cuisine refers to the native cuisine of the Saraiki people in South Punjab.

cambodian.name: Cambodian cuisine
cambodian.line: Cambodian cuisine is the national cuisine of Cambodia.

cham.name: Cham cuisine
cham.line: The Chams, or Champa people, are an Austronesian ethnic group in Southeast Asia and are the original inhabitants of central Vietnam and coastal Cambodia before the arrival of the Cambodians and Vietnamese, during the expansion of the Khmer Empire and the Vietnamese conquest of Champa.

karen.name: Karen cuisine
karen.line: The Karen, also known as the Kayin, are an ethnolinguistic group of peoples who speak Karenic languages and are indigenous to southern and southeastern Myanmar, including the Irrawaddy delta and Kayin State.

mon.name: Mon cuisine
mon.line: The Mon are an ethnic group who inhabit Lower Myanmar's Mon State, Kayin State, Kayah State, Tanintharyi Region, Bago Region, the Irrawaddy Delta, and several areas in Thailand.

thai.name: Thai cuisine
thai.line: Thai cuisine, the national cuisine of Thailand and of Thai people, places emphasis on lightly prepared dishes with aromatics and spicy heat.

lao.name: Lao cuisine
lao.line: Lao cuisine or Laotian cuisine is the national cuisine of Laos.

bruneian.name: Bruneian cuisine
bruneian.line: Bruneian cuisine concerns the cuisine of Brunei.

christmas island.name: Christmas Island cuisine
christmas island.line: The cuisine of Christmas Island can best be described as an eclectic combination of traditional Australian cuisine and Asian cuisine, particularly meals from Malaysia and Indonesia.

east timor.name: East Timor cuisine
east timor.line: The Cuisine of Timor-Leste consists of regional popular foods such as pork, fish, basil, tamarind, legumes, maize, rice, root vegetables, and tropical fruit.

filipino.name: Filipino cuisine
filipino.line: Filipino cuisine includes the food traditions of more than a hundred ethnolinguistic groups across the Philippine archipelago.

ilocano.name: Ilocano cuisine
ilocano.line: The Ilocano people, also referred to as Ilokáno, Ilóko, Ilúko, or Samtóy, are an Austronesian ethnolinguistic group native to the Philippines.

kapampangan.name: Kapampangan cuisine
kapampangan.line: Kapampangan cuisine differed noticeably from other groups in the Philippines.

tagalog.name: Tagalog cuisine
tagalog.line: The Tagalog people are an Austronesian ethnic group native to the Philippines, particularly the Metro Manila and Calabarzon regions and Marinduque province of southern Luzon, and comprise the majority in the provinces of Bulacan, Bataan, Nueva Ecija, Aurora, and Zambales in Central Luzon and the island of Mindoro.

malaysian.name: Malaysian cuisine
malaysian.line: Malaysian cuisine consists of cooking traditions and practices found in Malaysia, and reflects the multi-ethnic makeup of its population.

arab.name: Arab cuisine
arab.line: Arab cuisine refers to the regional culinary traditions of the Arab world, spanning the Maghreb and the Mashriq.

eurasian.name: Eurasian cuisine
eurasian.line: The Eurasian cuisine of Malaysia and Singapore is a type of fusion cuisine.

malay.name: Malay cuisine
malay.line: Malay cuisine is the traditional food of the Malays.

sabahan.name: Sabahan cuisine
sabahan.line: Sabahan cuisine is a regional cuisine of Malaysia.

sarawakian.name: Sarawakian cuisine
sarawakian.line: Sarawakian cuisine is a regional cuisine of Malaysia.

singaporean.name: Singaporean cuisine
singaporean.line: Singaporean cuisine is derived from several ethnic groups in Singapore and has developed through centuries of political, economic, and social changes in the cosmopolitan city-state.

acehnese.name: Acehnese cuisine
acehnese.line: Acehnese cuisine is the cuisine of the Acehnese people of Aceh in Sumatra, Indonesia.

balinese.name: Balinese cuisine
balinese.line: Balinese cuisine is a cuisine tradition of Balinese people from the volcanic island of Bali.

banjar.name: Banjar cuisine
banjar.line: Banjarese cuisine is the cooking tradition and cuisine of Banjar people of South Kalimantan in Indonesia.

batak.name: Batak cuisine
batak.line: Batak cuisine is the cuisine and cooking traditions of Batak ethnic groups, predominantly found in Northern Sumatra region, Indonesia.

indo.name: Indo cuisine
indo.line: Indo cuisine is a fusion cooking and cuisine tradition, mainly existing in Indonesia and the Netherlands, as well as Belgium, South Africa and Suriname.

indonesian arab.name: Indonesian Arab cuisine
indonesian arab.line: Arab Indonesian cuisine is characterized by the mixture of Middle Eastern cuisine with local Indonesian-style cuisine.

indonesian indian.name: Indonesian Indian cuisine
indonesian indian.line: Indian Indonesian cuisine is characterized by the mixture of Indian cuisine with local Indonesian-style.

javanese.name: Javanese cuisine
javanese.line: Javanese cuisine is the cuisine of Javanese people, a major ethnic group in Indonesia in the provinces of Central Java, Yogyakarta, and East Java.

betawi.name: Betawi cuisine
betawi.line: Betawi cuisine draws from a range of culinary traditions.

madurese.name: Madurese cuisine
madurese.line: Madurese cuisine is the culinary tradition of the Madurese people from Madura Island in Indonesia.

sundanese.name: Sundanese cuisine
sundanese.line: Sundanese cuisine is the cuisine of the Sundanese people of Western Java and Banten, Indonesia.

makassar.name: Makassar cuisine
makassar.line: Makassarese cuisine is the cuisine of Makassarese people of Makassar in the South Sulawesi province of Indonesia.

manado.name: Manado cuisine
manado.line: Minahasan cuisine or Manado cuisine is the cooking tradition of the Minahasan people of North Sulawesi, Indonesia.

palembang.name: Palembang cuisine
palembang.line: Palembangese cuisine is the cuisine of the Palembangese people of the city of Palembang in the South Sumatra province of Indonesia.

armenian.name: Armenian cuisine
armenian.line: Armenian cuisine includes the foods and cooking techniques of the Armenian people and traditional Armenian foods and drinks.

eastern arabian.name: Eastern Arabian cuisine
eastern arabian.line: Eastern Arabian cuisine, also called Khaleeji cuisine, is the traditional Arabic cuisine variant that is shared by the population in Eastern Arabia and areas around the Persian Gulf.

bahraini.name: Bahraini cuisine
bahraini.line: The cuisine of Bahrain consists of dishes such as biryani, harees, khabeesa, machboos, mahyawa, quzi and zalabia.

emirati.name: Emirati cuisine
emirati.line: Emirati cuisine is the local traditional Arabic cuisine of the United Arab Emirates.

kuwaiti.name: Kuwaiti cuisine
kuwaiti.line: Kuwaiti cuisine is an amalgamation of primarily Arabian and Iranian, with modern influences from Indian.

omani.name: Omani cuisine
omani.line: Omani cuisine is part of the Khaleeji cuisine and is influenced by Arab, Indian, Iranian, Asian, Greek, and African cuisine, reflecting Oman's position as a vast trading empire at the intersection of traditional spice trade routes.

qatari.name: Qatari cuisine
qatari.line: Qatari cuisine is made up of traditional Arab cuisine.

saudi arabian.name: Saudi Arabian cuisine
saudi arabian.line: Saudi Arabian cuisine is the cooking styles and dishes of Saudi Arabia.

yemeni.name: Yemeni cuisine
yemeni.line: Yemeni cuisine is distinct from the wider Middle Eastern cuisines with regional variation.

levantine.name: Levantine cuisine
levantine.line: Levantine cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Levant.

iraqi.name: Iraqi cuisine
iraqi.line: Iraqi cuisine is a Middle Eastern cuisine that has its origins in the ancient Near East culture of the Fertile Crescent.

israeli.name: Israeli cuisine
israeli.line: Israeli cuisine primarily comprises dishes brought from the Jewish diaspora, and has more recently been defined by the development of a notable fusion cuisine characterized by the mixing of Jewish cuisine and Arab cuisine.

ancient israelite.name: Ancient Israelite cuisine
ancient israelite.line: Ancient Israelite cuisine was similar to other contemporary Mediterranean cuisines.

jordanian.name: Jordanian cuisine
jordanian.line: Jordanian cuisine is a Levantine cuisine developed over time in Jordan.

lebanese.name: Lebanese cuisine
lebanese.line: Lebanese cuisine comprises the culinary traditions and practices originating from Lebanon.

mizrahi jewish.name: Mizrahi Jewish cuisine
mizrahi jewish.line: Mizrahi Jewish cuisine is an assortment of cooking traditions that developed among the Mizrahi Jewish communities of the Middle East, North Africa and Central Asia.

palestinian.name: Palestinian cuisine
palestinian.line: Palestinian cuisine consists of foods from or commonly eaten by Palestinians or in the region of Palestine, whether in Palestine, Israel, Jordan, or refugee camps in nearby countries, or by the Palestinian diaspora.

syrian.name: Syrian cuisine
syrian.line: Syrian cuisine is an Arab and Mediterranean cuisine that traces back to ancient civilization in Syria and the region.

syrian jewish.name: Syrian Jewish cuisine
syrian jewish.line: Syrian Jewish cuisine is the cuisine of Syrian Jews.

assyrian.name: Assyrian cuisine
assyrian.line: Assyrian cuisine is the cuisine of the indigenous Assyrian people, Eastern Aramaic-speaking Syriac Christians of Iraq, northeastern Syria, northwestern Iran and southeastern Turkey.

caucasian.name: Caucasian cuisine
caucasian.line: This article provides a list of dishes originating from the Caucasus.

azerbaijani.name: Azerbaijani cuisine
azerbaijani.line: Azerbaijani cuisine is a term describing the cooking styles and dishes of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

chechen.name: Chechen cuisine
chechen.line: Chechen cuisine encompasses the traditional cooking styles and dishes of the Chechen people of Chechnya and the Chechen diaspora.

circassian.name: Circassian cuisine
circassian.line: Circassian cuisine is an ethnic cuisine, based on the cooking style and traditions of the Circassian people of the North Caucasus.

georgian.name: Georgian cuisine
georgian.line: Georgian cuisine consists of cooking traditions, techniques, and practices of Georgia.

ossetian.name: Ossetian cuisine
ossetian.line: Ossetian cuisine refers to the cooking styles and dishes of the Ossetians of the Caucasus.

turkish.name: Turkish cuisine
turkish.line: Turkish cuisine encompasses the traditional and regional foods of Turkey and its diaspora.

pontic greek.name: Pontic Greek cuisine
pontic greek.line: Pontic Greek cuisine consists of foods traditionally eaten by Pontic Greeks, a Greek-speaking ethnic minority that originates from the southern shore of the Black Sea in modern Turkey.

ashkenazi jewish.name: Ashkenazi Jewish cuisine
ashkenazi jewish.line: Ashkenazi Jewish cuisine is an assortment of cooking traditions that was developed by the Ashkenazi Jews of Central, Eastern, Northwestern and Northern Europe, and their descendants, particularly in the United States and other Western countries.

austrian.name: Austrian cuisine
austrian.line: Austrian cuisine consists of many different local or regional cuisines.

viennese.name: Viennese cuisine
viennese.line: Viennese cuisine is the cuisine of Vienna, Austria.

czech.name: Czech cuisine
czech.line: Czech cuisine includes a variety of staples, dishes, beverages, and snacks which are typical of the broader Central European region.

moravian.name: Moravian cuisine
moravian.line: Moravian cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with Moravia, a region of the Czech Republic and historically belongs to the Moravia, former historical country in Central Europe.

hungarian.name: Hungarian cuisine
hungarian.line: Hungarian cuisine is the cuisine characteristic of the nation of Hungary, and its primary ethnic group, Hungarians.

liechtensteiner.name: Liechtensteiner cuisine
liechtensteiner.line: The cuisine of Liechtenstein is diverse, having been influenced by the cuisine of nearby countries, particularly Switzerland and Austria, as well as other countries in Central Europe.

polish.name: Polish cuisine
polish.line: Polish cuisine is a style of food preparation from Poland.

silesian.name: Silesian cuisine
silesian.line: Silesian cuisine belongs to the region of Silesia in Central Europe.

slovak.name: Slovak cuisine
slovak.line: Slovak cuisine varies slightly from region to region across Slovakia.

slovenian.name: Slovenian cuisine
slovenian.line: Slovenian cuisine is influenced by the diversity of Slovenia's landscape, climate, history and neighbouring cultures.

swiss.name: Swiss cuisine
swiss.line: Swiss cuisine is an ensemble of national, regional, and local dishes, consisting of the ingredients, recipes, and cooking techniques developed in Switzerland or assimilated from other cultures, particularly neighboring countries.

baden.name: Baden cuisine
baden.line: The cuisine of the German region of Baden is comparatively light and small among Germany's regional cuisines, but is regarded within the country as among the best.

bavarian.name: Bavarian cuisine
bavarian.line: Bavarian cuisine is a style of cooking from Bavaria, Germany.

brandenburg.name: Brandenburg cuisine
brandenburg.line: The cuisine of Brandenburg, a region of Germany, is considered rather down-to-earth compared to other cuisines.

franconian.name: Franconian cuisine
franconian.line: Franconian cuisine is an umbrella term for all dishes that nominally belong to the region of Franconia.

hamburg.name: Hamburg cuisine
hamburg.line: Due to its centuries-old history as a major port town the cuisine of Hamburg is very diversified and sapid as ingredients' supply was safe.

hessian.name: Hessian cuisine
hessian.line: Hessian cuisine is based on centuries-old recipes, and forms a major part of the Hesse identity.

lower saxon.name: Lower Saxon cuisine
lower saxon.line: Lower Saxon cuisine covers a range of regional, North German culinary traditions from the region correspondingly broadly to the state of Lower Saxony, which in many cases are very similar to one another, for example cuisine from the areas of Oldenburg, Brunswick, or East Frisia.

mecklenburg.name: Mecklenburg cuisine
mecklenburg.line: Mecklenburg cuisine is typically northeast German.

palatine.name: Palatine cuisine
palatine.line: The cuisine of the Palatinate region of Germany is essentially determined by regional dishes that have become popular throughout the whole region and even beyond.

pomeranian.name: Pomeranian cuisine
pomeranian.line: Pomeranian cuisine generally refers to dishes typical of the area that once formed the historic Province of Pomerania in northeast Germany and which included Stettin and Further Pomerania.

rhenish-hessian.name: Rhenish-Hessian cuisine
rhenish-hessian.line: Rhenish Hesse or Rhine Hesse is a region and a former government district in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

saxon.name: Saxon cuisine
saxon.line: Saxon cuisine encompasses regional cooking traditions of Saxony.

schleswig-holstein.name: Schleswig-Holstein cuisine
schleswig-holstein.line: The cuisine of Schleswig-Holstein forms part of the German cuisine in which the different influences of the regions Niedersachsen and Friesland and of Denmark are perceptible.

swabian.name: Swabian cuisine
swabian.line: Swabian cuisine is native to Swabia, a region in southwestern Germany comprising great parts of Württemberg and the Bavarian part of Swabia.

belarusian.name: Belarusian cuisine
belarusian.line: Belarusian cuisine refers to the culinary traditions native to Belarus and its people.

cossack.name: Cossack cuisine
cossack.line: Cossack cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Cossack people of present-day Ukraine and Russia.

komi.name: Komi cuisine
komi.line: Komi cuisine consists of the cuisine of the Komi Republic and the Komi peoples, and is characterized by the rich use of local foods.

mordovian.name: Mordovian cuisine
mordovian.line: Mordovian cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Mordovians, who now live in Mordovia and surrounding areas.

udmurt.name: Udmurt cuisine
udmurt.line: Udmurt cuisine consists of the cuisine of Udmurtia and the Udmurt people, and is characterized by the rich use of local foods.

ukrainian.name: Ukrainian cuisine
ukrainian.line: Ukrainian cuisine is the collection of the various cooking traditions of the people of Ukraine, one of the largest and most populous European countries.

crimean tatar.name: Crimean Tatar cuisine
crimean tatar.line: Crimean Tatar cuisine is primarily the cuisine of the Crimean Tatars, who live on the Crimean Peninsula.

odesite.name: Odesite cuisine
odesite.line: The cuisine of Odesa in Ukraine is influenced by cultures of various regions, including Ukrainian, Russian, Jewish, Crimean Tatar, Armenian, Bulgarian, Moldovan, Greek, Georgian, French, German and Italian cultures.

estonian.name: Estonian cuisine
estonian.line: Traditional Estonian cuisine has substantially been based on meat and potatoes, and on fish in coastal and lakeside areas.

latvian.name: Latvian cuisine
latvian.line: Latvian cuisine typically consists of agricultural products, with meat featuring in most main dishes.

lithuanian.name: Lithuanian cuisine
lithuanian.line: Lithuanian cuisine features products suited to the cool and moist northern climate of Lithuania: barley, potatoes, rye, beets, greens, berries, and mushrooms are locally grown, and dairy products are one of its specialties.

danish.name: Danish cuisine
danish.line: Danish cuisine originated from the peasant population's own local produce and was enhanced by cooking techniques developed in the late 19th century and the wider availability of goods during and after the Industrial Revolution.

faroese.name: Faroese cuisine
faroese.line: Important parts of Faroese cuisine are lamb and also fish owing to proximity to the sea.

new nordic.name: New Nordic cuisine
new nordic.line: New Nordic Cuisine is a culinary movement which has been developed in the Nordic countries, and Scandinavia in particular, since the mid-2000s.

finnish.name: Finnish cuisine
finnish.line: Finnish cuisine is notable for generally combining traditional country fare and haute cuisine with contemporary continental-style cooking.

icelandic.name: Icelandic cuisine
icelandic.line: The cuisine of Iceland has a long history.

norwegian.name: Norwegian cuisine
norwegian.line: Norwegian cuisine in its traditional form is based largely on the raw materials readily available in Norway.

sami.name: Sami cuisine
sami.line: Sámi cuisine is the cuisine of peoples from the Sápmi territory of the Sámi people, which spans Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia.

swedish.name: Swedish cuisine
swedish.line: Swedish cuisine is the traditional food of Sweden.

balkan.name: Balkan cuisine
balkan.line: Balkan cuisine encompasses the various cuisines of the Balkans region in Europe.

albanian.name: Albanian cuisine
albanian.line: Albanian cuisine is a representative of the cuisine of the Mediterranean.

kosovan.name: Kosovan cuisine
kosovan.line: The cuisine of Kosovo is a representative of the cuisine of the Balkans and consists of traditional dishes by ethnic groups native to Kosovo.

aromanian.name: Aromanian cuisine
aromanian.line: Aromanian cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Aromanians.

bosnian.name: Bosnian cuisine
bosnian.line: Bosnian cuisine is the traditional cuisine of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

bulgarian.name: Bulgarian cuisine
bulgarian.line: Bulgarian cuisine is part of the cuisine of Eastern Europe, sharing characteristics with other Balkan cuisines.

croatian.name: Croatian cuisine
croatian.line: Croatian cuisine is heterogeneous and is known as a cuisine of the regions, since every region of Croatia has its own distinct culinary tradition.

gagauz.name: Gagauz cuisine
gagauz.line: Gagauz cuisine refers to the culinary practices of the Gagauz people.

macedonian.name: Macedonian cuisine
macedonian.line: Macedonian cuisine is the cuisine of North Macedonia.

montenegrin.name: Montenegrin cuisine
montenegrin.line: Montenegrin cuisine is a result of Montenegro's geographic position and its long history and tradition.

serbian.name: Serbian cuisine
serbian.line: Serbian cuisine is a Balkan cuisine that consists of the culinary methods and traditions of Serbia.

romani.name: Romani cuisine
romani.line: Romani cuisine is diverse, reflecting the culinary traditions of the respective countries in which Romani people have lived for generations.

romanian.name: Romanian cuisine
romanian.line: Romanian cuisine is the traditional cuisine of Romania, shaped by the country's varied geography, pastoral traditions, and agricultural heritage.

moldovan.name: Moldovan cuisine
moldovan.line: Moldovan cuisine is a style of cooking related to the people of Moldova.

transylvanian saxon.name: Transylvanian Saxon cuisine
transylvanian saxon.line: The Transylvanian Saxon cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Transylvanian Saxons, a German ethnic group and minority which has been living in Transylvania as well as in other historical regions on the territory of present-day Romania since the mid-12th century onwards.

gibraltarian.name: Gibraltarian cuisine
gibraltarian.line: Gibraltarian cuisine is the result of a long relationship between the people of Spanish Andalusia and those of Great Britain, as well as the many foreigners who have made Gibraltar their home over the past three centuries.

greek.name: Greek cuisine
greek.line: Greek cuisine is the cuisine of Greece and the Greek diaspora.

cretan.name: Cretan cuisine
cretan.line: Cretan cuisine is the traditional cuisine of the Greek island of Crete.

cypriot.name: Cypriot cuisine
cypriot.line: Cypriot cuisine is the cuisine of the island of Cyprus.

epirotic.name: Epirotic cuisine
epirotic.line: Epirotic cuisine is the traditional Greek cuisine of the region of Epirus.

italian.name: Italian cuisine
italian.line: Italian cuisine is a Mediterranean cuisine consisting of the ingredients, recipes and cooking techniques developed in Italy since Roman times, and later spread around the world together with waves of Italian diaspora.

abruzzese and molisan.name: Abruzzese and Molisan cuisine
abruzzese and molisan.line: Cuisine of Abruzzo is eclectic, drawing on pastoral, mountain, and coastal cuisine.

arbëreshë.name: Arbëreshë cuisine
arbëreshë.line: The Arbëreshë cuisine is the cuisine of the Arbëreshë people who settled in southern Italy between the 15th and 18th centuries after successive migrations from Albania, Epirus, Chameria and Morea, during the Ottoman conquest of the Balkans.

basilicatan (lucanian).name: Basilicatan (Lucanian) cuisine
basilicatan (lucanian).line: The cuisine of Basilicata, or Lucanian cuisine, is the cuisine of the Basilicata region of Italy.

calabrian.name: Calabrian cuisine
calabrian.line: Calabria is a region in Southern Italy.

corsican.name: Corsican cuisine
corsican.line: The cuisine of Corsica is the traditional cuisine of the island of Corsica.

ligurian.name: Ligurian cuisine
ligurian.line: Ligurian cuisine consists of dishes from the culinary tradition of Liguria, a region of northwestern Italy, which makes use of ingredients linked both to local production, and to imports from areas with which, over the centuries, the Ligurians have had frequent trade.

lombard.name: Lombard cuisine
lombard.line: Lombard cuisine consists of the cooking traditions and practices of the Lombardy region.

mantuan.name: Mantuan cuisine
mantuan.line: Mantuan cuisine is the set of traditional dishes of the Italian province of Mantua, some of which date back to the time of the Gonzaga.

neapolitan.name: Neapolitan cuisine
neapolitan.line: Neapolitan cuisine has influences that date back to the Greco-Roman period.

pugliese.name: Pugliese cuisine
pugliese.line: Apulian cuisine is characterized above all by the importance given to raw materials, both land and sea, and by the fact that all the ingredients are designed to enhance and not alter the basic flavours of the products used.

sammarinese.name: Sammarinese cuisine
sammarinese.line: As San Marino is a microstate completely landlocked by Italy, Sammarinese cuisine is very similar to Italian cuisine, especially that of the adjoining Emilia-Romagna and Marche regions.

sardinian.name: Sardinian cuisine
sardinian.line: The cuisine of Sardinia is the traditional cuisine of the island of Sardinia.

sicilian.name: Sicilian cuisine
sicilian.line: Sicilian cuisine is the style of cooking on the island of Sicily.

tuscan.name: Tuscan cuisine
tuscan.line: Tuscan cuisine comprises the culinary traditions of the Tuscan region in Italy, celebrated for its simplicity and focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients like olive oil, legumes, and meats.

venetian.name: Venetian cuisine
venetian.line: Venetian cuisine, from the Veneto region, has a centuries-long history and differs significantly from other cuisines of northern Italy, and of neighbouring Austria and of Slavic countries, despite sharing some commonalities.

maltese.name: Maltese cuisine
maltese.line: Maltese cuisine reflects Maltese history, showing strong Italian influences, as well as influences from Spanish, French, Provençal and other Mediterranean cuisines, with some later British culinary influence.

monégasque.name: Monégasque cuisine
monégasque.line: Monégasque cuisine is the cuisine of the principality of Monaco.

occitan.name: Occitan cuisine
occitan.line: Occitan cuisine is the traditional cuisine and gastronomy of Occitania, the supranational region of southern Europe where Occitan is traditionally spoken.

portuguese.name: Portuguese cuisine
portuguese.line: Portuguese cuisine consists of the traditions and practices of cooking in Portugal.

spanish.name: Spanish cuisine
