spanish.line: Spanish cuisine consists of the traditions and practices of Spanish cooking.

andalusian.name: Andalusian cuisine
andalusian.line: Andalusian cuisine is the regional cuisine of Andalusia, Spain.

asturian.name: Asturian cuisine
asturian.line: Asturian cuisine refers to the typical dishes and ingredients found in the cuisine of the Asturias region of Spain.

aragonese.name: Aragonese cuisine
aragonese.line: The Aragonese cuisine includes several typical dishes and ingredients of the local cuisine of Aragon, a community in Spain.

balearic.name: Balearic cuisine
balearic.line: Balearic cuisine is a Mediterranean cuisine as cooked in the Balearic Islands, Spain.

basque.name: Basque cuisine
basque.line: Basque cuisine refers to the cuisine of the Basque Country and includes meats and fish grilled over hot coals, marmitako and lamb stews, cod, Tolosa bean dishes, paprikas from Lekeitio, pintxos, Idiazabal sheep's cheese, txakoli, and Basque cider.

canarian.name: Canarian cuisine
canarian.line: The cuisine of the Canary Islands draws influence from the Americas, North Africa, and Latin America, as well as the aboriginal inhabitants of the islands.

cantabrian.name: Cantabrian cuisine
cantabrian.line: Cantabrian cuisine is the cuisine from Cantabria, an autonomous community in northern Spain.

castilian-leonese.name: Castilian-Leonese cuisine
castilian-leonese.line: Castilian-Leonese cuisine refers to the typical dishes and ingredients of the region of Castile and León in Spain.

castilian-manchego.name: Castilian-Manchego cuisine
castilian-manchego.line: Manchego cuisine refers to the typical dishes and ingredients in the cuisine of the Castilla–La Mancha region of Spain.

catalan.name: Catalan cuisine
catalan.line: Catalan cuisine is the cooking traditions and practices from Catalonia.

andorran.name: Andorran cuisine
andorran.line: Catalan cuisine is the cooking traditions and practices from Catalonia.

extremaduran.name: Extremaduran cuisine
extremaduran.line: Extremadura, Spain is known for its different ways of preparing the Iberian pork and mutton.

galician.name: Galician cuisine
galician.line: Galician cuisine refers to the typical dishes and ingredients found in the cuisine of the autonomous community of Galicia, Spain.

leonese.name: Leonese cuisine
leonese.line: Leonese cuisine is a subcategory of Spanish cuisine from the Province of León.

minorcan.name: Minorcan cuisine
minorcan.line: Menorcan cuisine refers to the typical food and drink of Menorca.

valencian.name: Valencian cuisine
valencian.line: Valencian cuisine is a Mediterranean cuisine as cooked in the Valencian Community, Spain.

belgian.name: Belgian cuisine
belgian.line: Belgian cuisine is widely varied among regions, while also reflecting the cuisines of neighbouring France, Germany and the Netherlands.

dutch.name: Dutch cuisine
dutch.line: Dutch cuisine is formed from the cooking traditions and practices of the Netherlands.

frisian.name: Frisian cuisine
frisian.line: Frisian cuisine consists of the traditional recipes and cooking methods of the historic region of Frisia, which is in present-day Germany and the Netherlands.

limburgian.name: Limburgian cuisine
limburgian.line: Limburgisch cuisine, the cuisine of the Province of Limburg, is different from the Belgian and Dutch cuisines but also shares many similarities with these cuisines.

french.name: French cuisine
french.line: French cuisine is the cooking traditions and practices of France.

haute.name: Haute cuisine
haute.line: Haute cuisine or grande cuisine is a style of cooking characterised by meticulous preparation, elaborate presentation, and the use of high quality ingredients.

lyonnaise.name: Lyonnaise cuisine
lyonnaise.line: Lyonnaise cuisine refers to cooking traditions and practices centering on the area around the French city of Lyon and historical Lyonnais culinary traditions.

nouvelle.name: Nouvelle cuisine
nouvelle.line: Nouvelle cuisine is an approach to cooking and food presentation in French cuisine.

british.name: British cuisine
british.line: British cuisine consists of the cooking traditions and practices associated with the United Kingdom, including the regional cuisines of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

channel islands.name: Channel Islands cuisine
channel islands.line: Channel Islands cuisine is the cooking styles, traditions and recipes of the Crown dependencies of the Channel Islands, namely the Bailiwicks of Guernsey and of Jersey.

english.name: English cuisine
english.line: English cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with England.

cornish.name: Cornish cuisine
cornish.line: Cornish cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with the English county of Cornwall and the Cornish people.

devonian.name: Devonian cuisine
devonian.line: The cuisine of Devon in England has influenced, and been influenced, by other British cuisine.

dorset.name: Dorset cuisine
dorset.line: The cuisine of Dorset, a county in South West England, is characterised by a variety of, often simple, dishes which are sourced, or have traditionally been sourced, from the county itself.

northern irish.name: Northern Irish cuisine
northern irish.line: Northern Irish cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with Northern Ireland.

scottish.name: Scottish cuisine
scottish.line: Scottish cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with Scotland.

welsh.name: Welsh cuisine
welsh.line: Welsh cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with Wales.

irish.name: Irish cuisine
irish.line: Irish cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with the island of Ireland.

australian.name: Australian cuisine
australian.line: Australian cuisine is the food and cooking practices of Australia and its inhabitants.

tasmanian.name: Tasmanian cuisine
tasmanian.line: Tasmania is an island state of Australia.

new zealand.name: New Zealand cuisine
new zealand.line: The cuisine of New Zealand has historical influences from British cuisine and Māori culture.

fijian.name: Fijian cuisine
fijian.line: Fijian cuisine has long consisted of primarily foraged and farm-grown food.

new caledonian.name: New Caledonian cuisine
new caledonian.line: French cuisine is the cooking traditions and practices of France.

papua new guinean.name: Papua New Guinean cuisine
papua new guinean.line: The cuisine of Papua New Guinea comprises the traditional varied foods found in the eastern part of the New Guinea island.

solomon islands.name: Solomon Islands cuisine
solomon islands.line: Cuisine of the Solomon Islands has developed over 5,000 years of inhabitation and external influences.

vanuatuan.name: Vanuatuan cuisine
vanuatuan.line: The cuisine of Vanuatu incorporates fish, root vegetables such as taro and yams, fruits, and vegetables.

mariana islands.name: Mariana Islands cuisine
mariana islands.line: The cuisine of the Mariana Islands is largely made up of meat dishes, including pork, poultry, and meat from other land mammals.

marshallese.name: Marshallese cuisine
marshallese.line: Marshallese cuisine comprises the fare, foods, beverages and foodways of the Marshall Islands, including its food-related customs and traditions.

nauruan.name: Nauruan cuisine
nauruan.line: The cuisine of Nauru is the traditional cuisine of the island state on the Pacific Ocean.

palauan.name: Palauan cuisine
palauan.line: Palau, officially the Republic of Palau, is an island country located in the Micronesia subregion of Oceania in the western Pacific Ocean.

niuean.name: Niuean cuisine
niuean.line: Niue is an island in the Southern Pacific, mostly inhabited by Polynesians.

pascuense (easter island).name: Pascuense (Easter Island) cuisine
pascuense (easter island).line: Pascuense cuisine, otherwise known as Easter Island cuisine or Rapa Nui cuisine, incorporates the influences of the indigenous Rapa Nui people and Latin America.

pitcairn islands.name: Pitcairn Islands cuisine
pitcairn islands.line: The Pitcairn Islands, officially Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands, are a group of four volcanic islands in the southern Pacific Ocean that form the sole British Overseas Territory in the Pacific Ocean.

samoan.name: Samoan cuisine
samoan.line: The traditional culture of Samoa is a communal way of life based on Fa'a Samoa, the unique socio-political culture.

tuvaluan.name: Tuvaluan cuisine
tuvaluan.line: The cuisine of Tuvalu, a state in the Central Pacific, is based on the staple of coconut and the many species of fish found in the ocean and the lagoons of the atolls of Tuvalu.

wallis and futuna.name: Wallis and Futuna cuisine
wallis and futuna.line: Wallis and Futuna, an overseas territory of France in Oceania, has a rich Polynesian culture that is very similar to the cultures of its neighbouring nations Samoa and Tonga.

note by note.name: Note by Note cuisine
note by note.line: Note by Note cuisine is a style of cooking based on molecular gastronomy, created by French chemist Hervé This.

vegan.name: Vegan cuisine
vegan.line: Veganism is the practice of abstaining from the use of animal products and the consumption of animal source foods, and an associated philosophy that rejects the commodity status of animals.

vegetarian.name: Vegetarian cuisine
vegetarian.line: Vegetarian cuisine, also known as plant-based cuisine, is a style of cooking defined by the inclusion of grains, legumes, nuts, vegetables, fruits, dairy, and sometimes eggs, and by the exclusion of meat and animal tissue products.

indian vegetarian.name: Indian vegetarian cuisine
indian vegetarian.line: India has the world's largest number of vegetarians.

buddhist.name: Buddhist cuisine
buddhist.line: Buddhist cuisine is an Asian cuisine that is followed by monks and many believers from areas historically influenced by Mahayana Buddhism.

mangalorean catholic.name: Mangalorean Catholic cuisine
mangalorean catholic.line: Mangalorean Catholic cuisine is the cuisine of the Mangalorean Catholic community which is an important aspect of the culture of Mangalorean Catholics.

mennonite.name: Mennonite cuisine
mennonite.line: Mennonite cuisine is food associated with Mennonites, members of Christian denominations that came out of the Anabaptist movement in sixteenth-century Switzerland and Netherlands.

jewish.name: Jewish cuisine
jewish.line: Jewish cuisine refers to the worldwide cooking traditions of the Jewish people.

ancient egyptian.name: Ancient Egyptian cuisine
ancient egyptian.line: The cuisine of ancient Egypt encompasses the food and drink consumed by the ancient Egyptians throughout a span of over three thousand years, which retained many consistent traits until well into Greco-Roman times.

ancient greek.name: Ancient Greek cuisine
ancient greek.line: Ancient Greek cuisine was characterized by its frugality for most, reflecting agricultural hardship, but a great diversity of ingredients was known, and wealthy Greeks were known to celebrate with elaborate meals and feasts.

ancient roman.name: Ancient Roman cuisine
ancient roman.line: The cuisine of ancient Rome changed significantly over the duration of the civilization's existence.

byzantine.name: Byzantine cuisine
byzantine.line: Byzantine cuisine was the continuation of local ancient Greek cuisine, ancient Roman cuisine, and Mediterranean cuisine.

early modern european.name: Early modern European cuisine
early modern european.line: The cuisine of early modern Europe was a mix of dishes inherited from medieval cuisine combined with innovations that would persist in the modern era.

futurist.name: Futurist cuisine
futurist.line: Futurist meals comprised a cuisine and style of dining advocated by some members of the Futurist movement, particularly in Italy.

historical chinese.name: Historical Chinese cuisine
historical chinese.line: The history of Chinese cuisine is marked by both variety and change.

historical indian.name: Historical Indian cuisine
historical indian.line: The history of Indian cuisine consists of cuisine of the Indian subcontinent, which is rich and diverse.

maya.name: Maya cuisine
maya.line: Ancient Maya cuisine was varied and extensive.

medieval.name: Medieval cuisine
medieval.line: Medieval cuisine includes foods, eating habits, and cooking methods of various European cultures during the Middle Ages, which lasted from the 5th to the 15th century.

ottoman.name: Ottoman cuisine
ottoman.line: Ottoman cuisine is the cuisine of the Ottoman Empire and its continuation in the cuisines of Turkey, the Balkans, the Caucasus, the Middle East and Northern Africa.

soviet.name: Soviet cuisine
soviet.line: Soviet cuisine, the common cuisine of the Soviet Union, was formed by the integration of the various national cuisines of the Soviet Union, in the course of the formation of the Soviet people.

thirteen colonies.name: Thirteen Colonies cuisine
thirteen colonies.line: The cuisine of the Thirteen Colonies includes the foodways, culinary culture and cooking methods of the Colonial United States and its people.

american.name: American cuisine
american.line: American cuisine encompasses the cooking style and range of dishes prepared in the United States.

german.name: German cuisine
german.line: German cuisine consists of many different local or regional cuisines, reflecting the country's federal history.

pakistani.name: Pakistani cuisine
pakistani.line: Pakistani cuisine encompasses the traditional and regional foods of Pakistan and its diaspora, Central and West Asia.

chinese.name: Chinese cuisine
chinese.line: Chinese cuisine comprises cuisines originating from China, that varies with the country's large population and geographic diversity, as well as from Chinese people from other parts of the world.

indian.name: Indian cuisine
indian.line: Indian cuisine is not a single homogeneous entity, but consists of the regional cuisines native to the Indian subcontinent.

indonesian.name: Indonesian cuisine
indonesian.line: Indonesian cuisine is a collection of regional culinary traditions of the various ethnic groups that form the archipelagic nation of Indonesia.

adzuki-beans.name: Adzuki Beans
adzuki-beans.line: Vigna angularis, also known as the adzuki bean, azuki bean, aduki bean, red bean, or red mung bean, is an annual vine widely cultivated throughout East Asia for its small bean.

allspice.name: Allspice
allspice.line: Allspice, also known as Jamaica pepper, myrtle pepper, pimenta, or pimento, is the dried unripe berry of Pimenta dioica, a midcanopy tree native to the Greater Antilles, southern Mexico, and Central America, now cultivated in many warm parts of the world.

almonds.name: Almonds
almonds.line: The almond is a species of tree from the genus Prunus.

almond-flour.name: Almond Flour
almond-flour.line: Almond meal, almond flour or ground almond is made from ground sweet almonds.

apples.name: Apples
apples.line: An apple is the round, edible fruit of an apple tree.

artichokes.name: Artichokes
artichokes.line: The artichoke is a variety of a species of thistle cultivated as food.

asparagus.name: Asparagus
asparagus.line: Asparagus or garden asparagus is a perennial flowering plant species in the genus Asparagus native to Eurasia.

avocados.name: Avocados
avocados.line: The avocado, alligator pear or avocado pear is an evergreen tree in the laurel family.

bacon.name: Bacon
bacon.line: Bacon is a type of salt-cured pork made from various cuts, typically the belly or less fatty parts of the back.

baking-powder.name: Baking Powder
baking-powder.line: Baking powder is a dry chemical leavening agent, a mixture of a carbonate or bicarbonate and a weak acid.

baking-soda.name: Baking Soda
baking-soda.line: Sodium bicarbonate, commonly known as baking soda or bicarbonate of soda, or saleratus, is a chemical compound with the chemical formula NaHCO3.

bamboo-shoots.name: Bamboo shoots
bamboo-shoots.line: Bamboo shoots or bamboo sprouts are the edible shoots of many bamboo species including Bambusa vulgaris and Phyllostachys edulis.

bananas.name: Bananas
bananas.line: A banana is an elongated, edible fruit that is botanically a berry produced by several kinds of large treelike herbaceous flowering plants in the genus Musa.

barley.name: Barley
barley.line: Barley, a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.

bay-leaf.name: Bay Leaf
bay-leaf.line: Bay leaves are aromatic leaves commonly used as herbs in cooking many world cuisines; They come from various plants of species with distinctive flavours and fragrances as desired of those cuisines.

bean-sprouts.name: Bean sprouts
bean-sprouts.line: Sprouting is the natural process by which seeds or spores germinate and put out shoots, and already established plants produce new leaves or buds, or other structures experience further growth.

beef.name: Beef
beef.line: Beef is the culinary name for meat from cattle.

beets.name: Beets
beets.line: Beetroot or beet is the taproot portion of a Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris plant in the Conditiva Group.

bell-peppers.name: Bell peppers
bell-peppers.line: The bell pepper is the fruit of plants in the Grossum Group of the species Capsicum annuum.

black-pepper.name: Black Pepper
black-pepper.line: Black pepper is a flowering vine in the family Piperaceae, cultivated for its fruit, which is usually dried and used as a spice and seasoning.

breadcrumbs.name: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.line: Breadcrumbs are a culinary ingredient consisting of flour or crumbled bread of varying dryness, sometimes with seasonings added.

broccoli.name: Broccoli
broccoli.line: Broccoli is an edible green plant in the cabbage family whose large flowering head, stalk and small associated leaves are eaten as a vegetable.

brown-sugar.name: Brown Sugar
brown-sugar.line: Brown sugar is a sucrose sugar product with a distinctive brown color due to the presence of molasses.

bulgur.name: Bulgur
bulgur.line: Bulgur or borghol is a cracked wheat foodstuff found in Middle Eastern and South Asian cuisines, among others.

butter.name: Butter
butter.line: Butter is a dairy product made from the fat and protein components of churned cream.

buttermilk.name: Buttermilk
buttermilk.line: Buttermilk is a dairy drink made by adding lactic acid bacteria to milk to produce a fermented dairy drink.

cabbage.name: Cabbage
cabbage.line: Cabbage, comprising several cultivars of Brassica oleracea, is a leafy green, red, or white biennial plant grown as an annual vegetable crop for its dense-leaved heads.

caraway-seeds.name: Caraway Seeds
caraway-seeds.line: Caraway, also known as meridian fennel, is a biennial plant in the family Apiaceae, native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa.

cardamom.name: Cardamom
cardamom.line: Cardamom, sometimes cardamon or cardamum, is a spice made from the seeds of several plants in the genera Elettaria and Amomum in the family Zingiberaceae.

carp.name: Carp
carp.line: The term carp is a generic common name for numerous species of freshwater fish from the family Cyprinidae, a very large clade of ray-finned fish mostly native to Eurasia.

carrots.name: Carrots
carrots.line: The carrot is a root vegetable in the umbellifer family Apiaceae.

cassava.name: Cassava
cassava.line: Manihot esculenta, commonly called cassava, manioc, or yuca, is a woody shrub of the spurge family, Euphorbiaceae, native to South America, from Brazil, Paraguay and parts of the Andes.

cauliflower.name: Cauliflower
cauliflower.line: Cauliflower is a vegetable belonging to the species Brassica oleracea in the family Brassicaceae.

celery.name: Celery
celery.line: Celery is a cultivated plant belonging to the species Apium graveolens in the family Apiaceae that has been used as a vegetable since ancient times.

celery-root.name: Celery root
celery-root.line: Celeriac, also called celery root, knob celery, and turnip-rooted celery, is a group of cultivars of Apium graveolens cultivated for their edible bulb-like hypocotyl, and shoots.

chayote.name: Chayote
chayote.line: Chayote, also known as christophine, mirliton, güisquil, and choko, is an edible plant belonging to the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae.

cheese-cheddar.name: Cheddar cheese
cheese-cheddar.line: Cheddar cheese is a natural cheese that is relatively hard, off-white, and sometimes sharp-tasting.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.line: Cheese is a type of dairy product produced in a range of flavors, textures, and forms by curdling of milk, usually from cows, goats or sheep, and sometimes of water buffalo.

chestnuts.name: Chestnuts
chestnuts.line: Chestnuts are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea, in the beech family Fagaceae.

chicken.name: Chicken
chicken.line: The chicken is the domesticated subspecies of the red junglefowl, originally native to Southeast Asia.

chickpea-flour.name: Chickpea Flour
chickpea-flour.line: Chickpea flour, common varieties include besan or gram flour, is a pulse flour made from chana dal or chickpea flour or brown/kaala chana, a chickpea.

chili-oil.name: Chili Oil
chili-oil.line: Chili oil or chile oil is a condiment made from vegetable oil that has been infused with chili peppers.

chili-peppers.name: Chili Peppers
chili-peppers.line: Chili peppers, also spelled chile or chilli, are varieties of berry-fruit plants from the genus Capsicum, which are members of the nightshade family Solanaceae, cultivated for their pungency.

chili-powder.name: Chili powder
chili-powder.line: Chili powder is the dried, pulverized fruit of one or more varieties of chili pepper, sometimes with the addition of other spices.

chili-sauce.name: Chili sauce
chili-sauce.line: Chili sauce and chili paste are condiments prepared with chili peppers.

chocolate.name: Chocolate
chocolate.line: Chocolate is a food made from roasted and ground cocoa beans.

clams.name: Clams
clams.line: Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc.

cloves.name: Cloves
cloves.line: Cloves are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.

cocoa-powder.name: Cocoa Powder
cocoa-powder.line: Cocoa powder, often simply cocoa, is an aromatic powder derived from the seeds of the Theobroma cacao tree.

coconut-milk.name: Coconut Milk
coconut-milk.line: Coconut milk is a plant milk extracted from the grated pulp of mature coconuts.

coconut-oil.name: Coconut Oil
coconut-oil.line: Coconut oil is an edible oil derived from the meat of the coconut palm fruit.

cod.name: Cod
cod.line: Cod is the common name for the demersal fish genus Gadus, belonging to the family Gadidae.

coffee.name: Coffee
coffee.line: Coffee is a beverage brewed from roasted, ground coffee beans.

collard-greens.name: Collard greens
collard-greens.line: Collard is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea.

condensed-milk.name: Condensed milk
condensed-milk.line: Condensed milk is cow's milk from which water has been removed.

corn.name: Corn
corn.line: Maize, also known as corn, is a tall stout grass that produces cereal grain.

corn-tortillas.name: Corn tortillas
corn-tortillas.line: In Mexico and Central America, a corn tortilla or just tortilla is a type of thin, unleavened flatbread, made from hominy, that is the whole kernels of maize treated with alkali to improve their nutrition in a process called nixtamalization.

corned-beef.name: Corned beef
corned-beef.line: Corned beef is a salt-cured piece of beef.

cornmeal.name: Cornmeal
cornmeal.line: Cornmeal is a meal ground from dried maize.

cornstarch.name: Cornstarch
cornstarch.line: Corn starch, or cornflour is the starch powder derived from corn grain.

cottage-cheese.name: Cottage cheese
cottage-cheese.line: Cottage cheese is a type of fresh cheese with a mild flavor and a creamy, heterogeneous texture made from skimmed milk – hence the low milkfat content.

crab.name: Crab
crab.line: Crabs are decapod crustaceans, either the Brachyura or various groups within the closely related Anomura, characterised by having a heavily armoured shell, their tail segments concealed under the body, the ability to run sideways, and the habit of hiding in rocky crevices.

cream-cheese.name: Cream cheese
cream-cheese.line: Cream cheese is a soft, usually mild-tasting fresh cheese made from milk and cream.

cream-of-tartar.name: Cream of Tartar
cream-of-tartar.line: Potassium bitartrate, also known as potassium hydrogen tartrate, with formula KC4H5O6, is the potassium acid salt of tartaric acid—specifically, l--tartaric acid.

creme-fra-che.name: Crème Fraîche
creme-fra-che.line: Crème fraîche is a dairy product similar to sour cream; it is a soured cream containing 10–45% butterfat, with a pH of approximately 4.5.

cucumbers.name: Cucumbers
cucumbers.line: The cucumber is a widely-cultivated creeping vine plant in the family Cucurbitaceae that bears cylindrical to spherical fruits, used as culinary vegetables.

cumin.name: Cumin
cumin.line: Cumin is a flowering plant in the family Apiaceae, native to the Irano-Turanian Region.

curry-powder.name: Curry Powder
curry-powder.line: Curry powder is any of several spice mixes for curry, adapted from garam masala in Indian cuisine.

cuttlefish.name: Cuttlefish
cuttlefish.line: Cuttlefish, or cuttles, are marine molluscs of the family Sepiidae.

daikon.name: Daikon
daikon.line: Daikon or mooli is a mild-flavored winter radish usually characterized by fast-growing leaves and a long, white, napiform root.

dark-soy-sauce.name: Dark Soy Sauce
dark-soy-sauce.line: In Chinese cuisine, dark soy sauce is a dark-coloured soy sauce used mainly for adding colour and flavour to dishes.

dijon-mustard.name: Dijon Mustard
dijon-mustard.line: Dijon mustard is a traditional mustard from France.

doenjang.name: Doenjang
doenjang.line: Doenjang or soybean paste is a type of fermented bean paste made of soybean and brine used in Korean cuisine.

doubanjiang.name: Doubanjiang
doubanjiang.line: Doubanjiang, also known as douban, toban-djan, broad bean chili sauce, or fermented chili bean paste, is a hot and savory Chinese bean paste made from fermented broad beans, chili peppers, soybeans, salt, and flour.

dried-fruit.name: Dried fruit
dried-fruit.line: Dried fruit is fruit from which the majority of the original water content has been removed prior to cooking or being eaten on its own.

dried-shrimp.name: Dried Shrimp
dried-shrimp.line: Dried shrimp are shrimp that have been sun-dried and shrunk to a thumbnail size.

duck.name: Duck
duck.line: Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.

dumplings.name: Dumplings
dumplings.line: Dumplings are a broad class of dishes that consist of pieces of cooked dough, often wrapped around a filling.

durian.name: Durian
durian.line: The durian is the edible fruit of trees in the genus Durio, most often applying to those of Durio zibethinus, the only species available on the international market.

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.line: An egg is an organic vessel grown by an animal to carry a possibly fertilized egg cell – a zygote.

eggplant.name: Eggplant
eggplant.line: Solanum melongena is a plant species in the nightshade family Solanaceae, grown worldwide for its edible fruit, typically used as a vegetable in cooking.

farro.name: Farro
farro.line: Farro is a grain of any of three species of hulled wheat, namely einkorn, emmer, or spelt, sold dried and cooked in water until soft.

fennel.name: Fennel
fennel.line: Fennel is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.

feta.name: Feta
feta.line: Feta is a Greek white brined cheese made from sheep's milk or from a mixture of sheep and goat's milk.

fish.name: Fish
fish.line: A fish is an aquatic, anamniotic, gill-bearing vertebrate with a tough cranium to protect the brain.

fish-sauce.name: Fish Sauce
fish-sauce.line: Fish sauce is a liquid condiment made from fish or krill that have been coated in salt and fermented for up to two years.

five-spice-powder.name: Five-Spice Powder
five-spice-powder.line: Five-spice powder is a spice mixture of five or more spices—commonly star anise, cloves, Chinese cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, and fennel seeds—used predominantly in almost all branches of Chinese cuisine.

flour-tortillas.name: Flour tortillas
flour-tortillas.line: A flour tortilla or wheat tortilla is a tortilla made from finely ground wheat flour.

galangal.name: Galangal
galangal.line: Galangal is a rhizome of plants in the ginger family Zingiberaceae, with culinary and medicinal uses originating in Indonesia.

garam-masala.name: Garam Masala
garam-masala.line: Garam masala is a blend of ground spices originating in the Indian Subcontinent.

garlic.name: Garlic
garlic.line: Garlic is a species of bulbous flowering plants in the genus Allium.

gelatin.name: Gelatin
gelatin.line: Gelatin in American English or gelatine in British English is a translucent, colorless, flavorless food ingredient, commonly derived from partial hydrolysis of collagen taken from animal body parts.

ghee.name: Ghee
ghee.line: Ghee is a type of clarified butter, originating in the South Asia.

ginger.name: Ginger
ginger.line: Ginger is a flowering plant whose rhizome, ginger root or ginger, is widely used as a spice and a folk medicine.

glutinous-rice.name: Glutinous Rice
glutinous-rice.line: Glutinous rice is a type of rice grown mainly in Southeast Asia and the northeastern regions of South Asia, which has opaque grains and very low amylose content and is especially sticky when cooked.

gochujang.name: Gochujang
gochujang.line: Gochujang or red chili paste is a savory, sweet, and spicy fermented condiment popular in Korean cooking.

grapes.name: Grapes
grapes.line: A grape is a fruit, botanically a berry, of the deciduous woody vines of the flowering plant genus Vitis.

gravy.name: Gravy
gravy.line: Gravy is a sauce made from the juices of meats and vegetables that run naturally during cooking and often thickened with thickeners for added texture.

green-beans.name: Green Beans
green-beans.line: Green beans are young, unripe fruits of various cultivars of the common bean.

peas.name: Green peas
peas.line: Pea is a pulse or fodder crop, but the word often refers to the seed or sometimes the pod of this flowering plant species.

beef-ground.name: Ground beef
beef-ground.line: Ground beef, hamburger meat, minced beef or beef mince is beef that has been finely chopped with a knife or meat grinder, i.e., mincer or mincing machine.

guacamole.name: Guacamole
guacamole.line: Guacamole, sometimes informally shortened to guac in the United States, is an avocado-based dip, spread, or salad first developed in Mexico.

ham.name: Ham
ham.line: Ham is pork from a leg cut that has been preserved by wet or dry curing, with or without smoking.

harissa.name: Harissa
harissa.line: Harissa is a Tunisian hot chili pepper paste.

hazelnuts.name: Hazelnuts
hazelnuts.line: The hazelnut is the fruit of the hazel tree and therefore includes any of the nuts deriving from species of the genus Corylus, especially the nuts of the species Corylus avellana.

hoisin-sauce.name: Hoisin Sauce
hoisin-sauce.line: Hoisin sauce is a thick, savory sauce originating in China.

honey.name: Honey
honey.line: Honey is a sweet and viscous foodstuff made by several species of bees, the best-known of which are honey bees.

horseradish.name: Horseradish
horseradish.line: Horseradish is a perennial plant of the family Brassicaceae.

hot-dogs.name: Hot dogs
hot-dogs.line: A hot dog is a grilled, steamed, or boiled sausage served in the slit of a partially sliced bun.

hummus.name: Hummus
hummus.line: Hummus is a Levantine dip, spread, or savory dish made from cooked, mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, and garlic.

lettuce-iceberg.name: Iceberg lettuce
lettuce-iceberg.line: Iceberg lettuce, also called crisphead lettuce, is a common cultivar of lettuce.

jackfruit.name: Jackfruit
jackfruit.line: The jackfruit or jakfruit is a fruit tree in the mulberry family of Moraceae.

jam.name: Jam
jam.line: Fruit preserves are preparations of fruits whose main preserving agent is sugar and sometimes acid, often stored in glass jars and used as a condiment or spread.

juice.name: Juice
juice.line: Juice is a drink made from the extraction or pressing of the natural liquid contained in fruit and vegetables.

kasuri-methi.name: Kasuri Methi
kasuri-methi.line: Fenugreek is an annual plant in the family Fabaceae, which includes beans, peas, and peanuts.

katsuobushi.name: Katsuobushi
katsuobushi.line: Katsuobushi is simmered, smoked and fermented skipjack tuna.

ketchup.name: Ketchup
ketchup.line: Ketchup or catsup is a table condiment with a sweet and sour flavor.

kosher-salt.name: Kosher Salt
kosher-salt.line: Kosher salt or kitchen salt is coarse edible salt usually without common additives such as iodine, typically used in cooking and not at the table.

lard.name: Lard
lard.line: Lard is a semi-solid white fat product obtained by rendering the fatty tissue of a pig.

leafy-greens.name: Leafy greens
leafy-greens.line: Leaf vegetables, also called leafy greens, vegetable greens, or simply greens, are plant leaves eaten as a vegetable.

leeks.name: Leeks
leeks.line: A leek is a biennial vegetable, a cultivar of Allium ampeloprasum, the broadleaf wild leek.

lemons.name: Lemons
lemons.line: The lemon is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.

lemongrass.name: Lemongrass
lemongrass.line: Cymbopogon, also known as lemongrass, barbed wire grass, silky heads, oily heads, Cochin grass, Malabar grass, citronella grass or fever grass, is a genus of Asian, African, Australian, and tropical island plants in the grass family.

lentils.name: Lentils
lentils.line: The lentil is an annual legume grown for its lens-shaped edible seeds or pulses, also called lentils.

lettuce.name: Lettuce
lettuce.line: Lettuce is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.

long-beans.name: Long beans
long-beans.line: The asparagus bean is a legume cultivated for its edible green pods containing immature seeds, like the green bean.

lunch-meat.name: Lunch meat
lunch-meat.line: Lunch meats—also known as cold cuts, luncheon meats, cooked meats, sliced meats, cold meats, sandwich meats, delicatessens, and deli meats—are cooked or cured meats that are sliced and served cold or hot.

maltose.name: Maltose
maltose.line: Maltose, also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an α bond.

mango.name: Mango
mango.line: A mango is an edible stone fruit produced by the tropical tree Mangifera indica.

maple-syrup.name: Maple Syrup
maple-syrup.line: Maple syrup is a sweet syrup made from the sap of maple trees.

margarine.name: Margarine
margarine.line: Margarine is a spread used for flavoring, baking, and cooking.

mayonnaise.name: Mayonnaise
mayonnaise.line: Mayonnaise, colloquially referred to as "mayo", is a thick, creamy sauce with a rich and tangy taste that is commonly used on sandwiches, hamburgers, bound salads, and French fries.

meatballs.name: Meatballs
meatballs.line: A meatball is ground meat rolled into a large somewhat spherical ball, sometimes along with other ingredients, such as bread crumbs, minced onion, eggs, butter, and seasoning.

melon.name: Melon
melon.line: A melon is any of various plants of the family Cucurbitaceae with sweet, edible, and fleshy fruit.

milk.name: Milk
milk.line: Milk is usually a white liquid food produced by the mammary glands of lactating mammals.

milkfish.name: Milkfish
milkfish.line: The milkfish is a widespread species of ray-finned fish found throughout the Indo-Pacific.

millet.name: Millet
millet.line: Millets are a highly varied group of small-seeded grasses, widely grown around the world as a staple cereal crop.

mirin.name: Mirin
mirin.line: Mirin is a type of rice wine and a common ingredient in Japanese cooking.

miso.name: Miso
miso.line: Miso is a traditional Japanese seasoning.

mochiko.name: Mochiko
mochiko.line: Rice flour is a form of flour made from finely milled rice.

mung-beans.name: Mung Beans
mung-beans.line: The mung bean or green gram is a plant species in the legume family.

mushrooms.name: Mushrooms
mushrooms.line: A mushroom is the fleshy, spore-bearing fruiting body of a fungus, typically produced above ground on soil or another food source.

mussels.name: Mussels
mussels.line: Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.

napa-cabbage.name: Napa Cabbage
napa-cabbage.line: Napa cabbage is a type of Chinese cabbage originating near the Beijing region of China that is widely used in East Asian cuisine.

noodles.name: Noodles
noodles.line: Noodles are a type of food typically made from unleavened dough which is rolled flat and cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips or strings.

nori.name: Nori
nori.line: Nori is a dried edible seaweed used in Japanese cuisine, usually made from species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.

nutmeg.name: Nutmeg
nutmeg.line: Nutmeg is the seed, or the ground spice derived from the seed, of several tree species of the genus Myristica; fragrant nutmeg or true nutmeg is a dark-leaved evergreen tree cultivated for two spices derived from its fruit: nutmeg, from its seed, and mace, from the seed covering.

oats.name: Oats
oats.line: The oat, sometimes called the common oat, is a species of cereal grass grown for fodder and for its seed, which is known by the same name.

octopus.name: Octopus
octopus.line: An octopus is a soft-bodied, eight-limbed mollusc of the order Octopoda.

okra.name: Okra
okra.line: Okra, Abelmoschus esculentus, known in some English-speaking countries as lady's fingers, is a flowering plant in the mallow family native to West Africa.

olives.name: Olives
olives.line: The cultivated olive is a subspecies of subtropical evergreen tree in the family Oleaceae.

olive-oil.name: Olive Oil
olive-oil.line: Olive oil is a vegetable oil obtained by pressing whole olives and extracting the oil.

onion.name: Onion
onion.line: The onion, also known as the bulb onion or common onion, is a vegetable that is the most widely cultivated species of the genus Allium.

oxtail.name: Oxtail
oxtail.line: Oxtail is the culinary name for the tail of cattle.

oysters.name: Oysters
oysters.line: Oyster is the common name for a number of different families of salt-water bivalve molluscs that live in marine or brackish habitats.

oyster-sauce.name: Oyster Sauce
oyster-sauce.line: Oyster sauce describes a number of sauces made by cooking oysters.

palm-sugar.name: Palm Sugar
palm-sugar.line: Palm sugar is a sweetener derived from any variety of palm tree.

panko.name: Panko
panko.line: Breadcrumbs are a culinary ingredient consisting of flour or crumbled bread of varying dryness, sometimes with seasonings added.

papaya.name: Papaya
papaya.line: The papaya is the plant species Carica papaya, one of the 3 accepted species in the genus Carica of the family Caricaceae.

paprika.name: Paprika
paprika.line: Paprika is a spice made from dried and ground red peppers, Capsicum annuum.

parmesan.name: Parmesan
parmesan.line: Parmesan is an Italian hard, granular cheese produced from cow's milk and aged at least 12 months.

parsnips.name: Parsnips
parsnips.line: The parsnip is a root vegetable closely related to carrot and parsley, all belonging to the flowering plant family Apiaceae.

peanuts.name: Peanuts
peanuts.line: The peanut, also known as the groundnut, goober, goober pea, pindar or monkey nut, is a legume crop grown mainly for its edible seeds, contained in underground pods.

pears.name: Pears
pears.line: Pears are a genus of trees, Pyrus, in the family Rosaceae, that bear an edible apple-like fruit of the same name.

pine-nuts.name: Pine Nuts
pine-nuts.line: Pine nuts, also called piñón, pinoli, or pignoli, are the edible seeds of pines.

pineapple.name: Pineapple
pineapple.line: The pineapple is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

pistachios.name: Pistachios
pistachios.line: The pistachio is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.

pita.name: Pita
pita.line: Pita or pitta, also known as Greek bread, Arabic bread, Arab bread, Syrian bread, Lebanese bread, and pocket bread, is a family of yeast-leavened round flatbreads baked from wheat flour, common in the Mediterranean, Middle East, and neighboring areas.

plums.name: Plums
plums.line: A plum is a fruit of some species in Prunus subg.

pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
pomegranate.line: The pomegranate is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub or tree in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5 and 5 metres tall.

poppy-seeds.name: Poppy Seeds
poppy-seeds.line: Poppy seeds are a type of oilseed obtained from the poppy plant.

pork.name: Pork
pork.line: Pork is the culinary name for the meat of the pig.

pork-belly.name: Pork Belly
pork-belly.line: Pork belly or belly pork is a boneless, fatty primal cut of pork from the belly of a pig.

pork-chops.name: Pork chops
pork-chops.line: A pork chop is a thick slice of meat cut from the domestic pig, particularly one adjacent to a rib and usually served with it.

pork-jowl.name: Pork jowl
pork-jowl.line: Pork jowl is a cut of pork from a pig's cheek.

pork-loin.name: Pork loin
pork-loin.line: Pork loin is a primal cut of meat from a pig, created from the tissue along the dorsal side of the rib cage.

potato-starch.name: Potato Starch
potato-starch.line: Potato starch is starch extracted from potatoes.

powdered-sugar.name: Powdered Sugar
powdered-sugar.line: Powdered sugar, also called confectioners' sugar and icing sugar, is a finely ground sugar produced by milling granulated sugar into a powdered state.

puff-pastry.name: Puff Pastry
puff-pastry.line: Puff pastry, also known as pâte feuilletée, is a light, flaky pastry, its base dough composed of wheat flour and water.

quinoa.name: Quinoa
quinoa.line: Quinoa is a flowering plant in the amaranth family.

raisins.name: Raisins
raisins.line: A raisin is a dried grape.

raspberries.name: Raspberries
raspberries.line: The raspberry is the edible fruit of several plant species in the genus Rubus of the rose family, most of which are in the subgenus Idaeobatus, and these plants themselves.

red-bean-paste.name: Red Bean Paste
red-bean-paste.line: Red bean paste or red bean jam, also called adzuki bean paste or anko, is a paste made of red beans, used in East Asian cuisine.

refried-beans.name: Refried beans
refried-beans.line: Refried beans is a dish of cooked and mashed beans that is a traditional staple of Mexican and Tex-Mex cuisines, although each cuisine has a different approach when making the dish.

rice.name: Rice
rice.line: Rice is a cereal grain and, in its domesticated form, is the staple food of over half of the world's population, particularly in Africa and Asia.

rice-flour.name: Rice flour
rice-flour.line: Rice flour is a form of flour made from finely milled rice.

rice-noodles.name: Rice noodles
rice-noodles.line: Rice noodles are noodles made with rice flour and water as the principal ingredients.

rice-vermicelli.name: Rice vermicelli
rice-vermicelli.line: Rice vermicelli is a thin form of rice noodle.

lettuce-romaine.name: Romaine lettuce
lettuce-romaine.line: Romaine or cos lettuce is a variety of lettuce that grows in a tall head of sturdy dark green leaves with firm ribs down their centers.

rutabaga.name: Rutabaga
rutabaga.line: Rutabaga or swede is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus.

saffron.name: Saffron
saffron.line: Saffron is a spice derived from the sterile autumn-blooming flower of Crocus sativus, commonly known as the "saffron crocus".

sake.name: Sake
sake.line: Sake, saké, or saki, also referred to as Japanese rice wine, is an alcoholic beverage of Japanese origin made by fermenting rice that has been polished to remove the bran.

salami.name: Salami
salami.line: Salami is a salume consisting of fermented and air-dried meat, typically pork.

salmon.name: Salmon
salmon.line: Salmon are any of several commercially important species of ray-finned fish that can live in either freshwater or saltwater from the genera Salmo and Oncorhynchus of the family Salmonidae, native to tributaries of the North Atlantic and North Pacific basins.

salt-cod.name: Salt Cod
salt-cod.line: Dried and salted cod, sometimes referred to as salt cod or saltfish or salt dolly, is cod which has been preserved by drying after salting.

sauerkraut.name: Sauerkraut
sauerkraut.line: Sauerkraut is finely cut raw white cabbage that has been fermented by various lactic acid bacteria.

sausage.name: Sausage
sausage.line: A sausage is a type of meat product usually made from ground meat—often pork, beef, or poultry—along with salt, spices and other flavourings.

scallops.name: Scallops
scallops.line: Scallop is a common name that encompasses various species of marine bivalve molluscs in the taxonomic family Pectinidae, the scallops.

semolina.name: Semolina
semolina.line: Semolina is a coarse flour traditionally made from durum wheat.

sesame-oil.name: Sesame Oil
sesame-oil.line: Sesame oil is an edible vegetable oil derived from sesame seeds.

shallot.name: Shallot
shallot.line: The shallot is a cultivar group of the onion.

shaoxing-wine.name: Shaoxing Wine
shaoxing-wine.line: Shaoxing wine is a variety of Chinese Huangjiu made by fermenting glutinous rice, water, and wheat-based yeast.

shellfish.name: Shellfish
shellfish.line: Shellfish, in colloquial and fisheries usage, are exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms.

shrimp.name: Shrimp
shrimp.line: A shrimp is a common name typically used for crustaceans with an elongated body and a primarily swimming mode of locomotion.

shrimp-paste.name: Shrimp Paste
shrimp-paste.line: Shrimp paste, shrimp sauce, or prawn sauce is a fermented condiment commonly used in Southeast Asian and coastal Chinese cuisines.

sour-cream.name: Sour cream
sour-cream.line: Sour cream is a dairy product obtained by fermenting regular cream with certain kinds of lactic acid bacteria.

soy-milk.name: Soy milk
soy-milk.line: Soy milk, also known as soya milk, is a plant-based milk produced by soaking and grinding soybeans, boiling the mixture, and filtering out remaining particulates.

soy-sauce.name: Soy Sauce
soy-sauce.line: Soy sauce is a liquid condiment of Chinese origin, traditionally made from a fermented paste of soybeans, roasted grain, brine, and Aspergillus oryzae or Aspergillus sojae molds.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.line: Spinach is a leafy green flowering plant native to Central and Western Asia.

strawberries.name: Strawberries
strawberries.line: The garden strawberry is a widely grown hybrid plant cultivated worldwide for its fruit.

sugar.name: Sugar
sugar.line: Sugar is a class of sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates, many of which are used in food.

tahini.name: Tahini
tahini.line: Tahini is a Middle Eastern condiment made from ground sesame seeds.

tapioca-pearls.name: Tapioca pearls
tapioca-pearls.line: A tapioca pearl, also known as a tapioca ball, is an edible translucent sphere produced from tapioca, a starch made from the cassava root.

taro.name: Taro
taro.line: Taro, also known as dasheen, is a root vegetable.

tea.name: Tea
tea.line: Tea is an aromatic beverage prepared by infusion of hot or boiling fresh water with fresh or cured leaves of Camellia sinensis, an evergreen shrub native to East Asia that originated in the borderlands of southwestern China, northeast India and northern Myanmar.

tempeh.name: Tempeh
tempeh.line: Tempeh or tempe is a traditional Indonesian food made from fermented soybeans.

thai-basil.name: Thai Basil
thai-basil.line: Thai basil is a type of basil native to and widely used throughout Southeast Asia, that has been cultivated to provide distinctive traits.

tomato-paste.name: Tomato Paste
tomato-paste.line: Tomato paste is a thick paste made from tomatoes, which are cooked for several hours to reduce water content.

tomatoes.name: Tomatoes
tomatoes.line: The tomato is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.

tortillas.name: Tortillas
tortillas.line: A tortilla is a thin, circular unleavened flatbread, originally made from corn but now also made of wheat flour.

trout.name: Trout
trout.line: Trout is a generic common name for numerous species of carnivorous freshwater fishes belonging to the genera Oncorhynchus, Salmo, and Salvelinus, all of which are members of the subfamily Salmoninae in the family Salmonidae.

tuna.name: Tuna
tuna.line: Tuna are saltwater fish belonging to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the mackerel family.

turmeric.name: Turmeric
turmeric.line: Turmeric, or Curcuma longa, is a flowering plant in the ginger family Zingiberaceae.

turnips.name: Turnips
turnips.line: The turnip or white turnip is a root vegetable commonly grown in temperate climates worldwide for its white, fleshy taproot.

unagi.name: Unagi
unagi.line: Unagi is the Japanese word for freshwater eel, particularly the Japanese eel, Anguilla japonica.

vanilla-extract.name: Vanilla Extract
vanilla-extract.line: Vanilla extract is a solution made by macerating and percolating vanilla pods in a solution of ethanol and water.

veal.name: Veal
veal.line: Veal is the meat of calves, in contrast to the beef from older cattle.

vinegar.name: Vinegar
vinegar.line: Vinegar is an odorous aqueous solution of diluted acetic acid and trace compounds that may include flavorings or naturally occurring organic compounds.

walnuts.name: Walnuts
walnuts.line: A walnut is the edible seed of any tree of the genus Juglans, most often the Persian or English walnut, Juglans regia.

water-spinach.name: Water spinach
water-spinach.line: Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.

wheat-flour.name: Wheat Flour
wheat-flour.line: Wheat flour is a powder made from the grinding of common wheat used for human consumption.

worcestershire-sauce.name: Worcestershire Sauce
worcestershire-sauce.line: Worcestershire sauce or Worcester sauce is a fermented condiment invented by the pharmacists John Wheeley Lea and William Henry Perrins in Worcester, Worcestershire, England, during the first half of the 19th century.

yeast.name: Yeast
yeast.line: A yeast is any species of fungus that grows primarily in a unicellular form and reproduces via budding or fission.

onions-yellow.name: Yellow onions
onions-yellow.line: The yellow onion or brown onion is a variety of dry onion with a strong flavor.

yogurt.name: Yogurt
yogurt.line: Yogurt, also spelled yoghurt, is a food produced by bacterial fermentation of milk.

zucchini.name: Zucchini
zucchini.line: Zucchini, courgette, or Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica is a summer squash, a vining herbaceous plant whose fruit are harvested when their immature seeds and epicarp are still soft and edible.
